nodes.summary: Builds the least-violation programme whose positive optimum shows a linear problem infeasible.

nodes.name: check_infeasible
nodes.summary: Checks the least-violation programme's answer and duals as a certificate of infeasibility.

nodes.name: ray_problem
nodes.summary: Builds the recession-cone programme over a unit box whose strictly improving optimum is an improving ray.

nodes.name: check_ray
nodes.summary: Checks that a direction keeps every constraint and strictly improves the objective.

nodes.name: check_unbounded
nodes.summary: Checks unboundedness from a feasible point plus an improving ray.

nodes.name: check_cp
nodes.summary: Checks a constraint-model answer: whole-number values, linear constraints, all-different groups, objective and bound.

nodes.name: check_knapsack
nodes.summary: Checks that chosen knapsack items keep every capacity and recomputes their value.

nodes.name: check_job_shop
nodes.summary: Checks a job-shop schedule: task order within jobs, no machine overlap, and the recomputed makespan against the bound.

nodes.name: _negative_cycle
nodes.summary: Bellman-Ford search for a negative cycle in a residual network, used to show assignment and min-cost flow optimality.

nodes.name: check_assignment
nodes.summary: Checks an assignment is a valid matching avoiding forbidden pairs, recomputes its cost and shows optimality by no negative residual cycle.

nodes.name: _balance
nodes.summary: Checks arc capacities and computes each node's net flow for flow-conservation checks.

nodes.name: check_max_flow
nodes.summary: Checks a maximum flow's capacities and conservation and that the reported cut has exactly the flow's capacity, proving maximality.

nodes.name: check_min_cost_flow
nodes.summary: Checks a min-cost flow keeps capacities and supplies, recomputes its cost and shows optimality by no negative residual cycle.

nodes.name: check_routes
nodes.summary: Checks vehicle routes: each node visited once, depot start and end, loads within capacity, time windows met and distance recomputed.

nodes.name: _job_shop
nodes.summary: One CP-SAT solve of the job shop with interval variables, returning task starts, makespan and bound.

nodes.name: _schedule
nodes.summary: Runs the job-shop solve, checks the schedule and classifies the outcome for labelling.

nodes.name: solve_knapsack
nodes.summary: Public op: chooses items of most total value within every capacity, checked before it is reported.

nodes.name: solve_job_shop
nodes.summary: Public op: schedules jobs on machines minimising makespan on CP-SAT, checked before it is reported.

nodes.name: ortools
nodes.summary: Imports an OR-Tools module only when an op runs, ignoring the SWIG DeprecationWarning that otherwise crashes Python 3.12 under -W error.

nodes.name: version
nodes.summary: Returns the installed OR-Tools version.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Validates input data into a problem model, raising a Refusal with G6_E_OPTIM_INPUT_INVALID on failure.

nodes.name: time_limit
nodes.summary: Validates a time limit as a positive finite number of seconds within the maximum.

nodes.name: at_most
nodes.summary: Refuses with G6_E_OPTIM_INPUT_TOO_LARGE when a count exceeds its cap.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs an op's work and labels the outcome through envelope.finish, turning refusals and unforeseen engine failures into blocked results.

nodes.name: Refusal
nodes.summary: Exception carrying a stable G6_E_OPTIM code and reason for an op refused before or during solving.

nodes.name: finish
nodes.summary: Labels an optimisation result: blocked-escalated with no solution when a code is set, else qualified-draft only when G6's check passed, with the matching warning card.

nodes.name: _answer_card
nodes.summary: Builds the warning card for a solver answer: what G6 checked, and whether optimality rests on the solver or a gap remains.

nodes.name: _search_card
nodes.summary: Builds the warning card for a search answer: local optimum, best found or not converged, and what the claim rests on.

nodes.name: _assignment
nodes.summary: One linear sum assignment solve, padding the shorter side with free dummy rows and dropping them from the answer.

nodes.name: _assign
nodes.summary: Runs the assignment solve and checks its answer before labelling.

nodes.name: _max_flow
nodes.summary: One maximum-flow solve returning each arc's flow, the value and the source side of a minimum cut.

nodes.name: _min_cost_flow
nodes.summary: One minimum-cost flow solve returning each arc's flow and the total cost.

nodes.name: _routing
nodes.summary: One OR-Tools routing search with optional capacities and time windows, returning each vehicle's route and total distance.

nodes.name: _route
nodes.summary: Runs the routing search, checks the routes and reports them as not proven optimal.

nodes.name: solve_assignment
nodes.summary: Public op: pairs rows with columns at least total cost, with optimality shown by the residual network.

nodes.name: solve_max_flow
nodes.summary: Public op: maximum flow from source to sink with a minimum cut of equal capacity.

nodes.name: solve_min_cost_flow
nodes.summary: Public op: cheapest flow meeting node supplies within arc capacities.

nodes.name: solve_routing
nodes.summary: Public op: vehicle routing with optional demands, capacities and time windows, checked and not proven optimal.

nodes.name: SearchProblem
nodes.summary: The variables of a non-linear search, each with finite bounds and whole-number bounds for integer ones.

nodes.name: _Parser
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON expression tree into nodes, enforcing allowed operations, declared variables, node and depth limits and finite constants.

nodes.name: _Objective
nodes.summary: The callable a search evaluates: the compiled objective in the search's sense, counted and bounded in evaluations and time, remembering the best point.

nodes.name: parse_expression
nodes.summary: Parses a caller's JSON expression over named variables into G6's expression tree.

nodes.name: interpret
nodes.summary: Evaluates an expression tree at a point with G6's own interpreter, the path used to re-check answers.

nodes.name: _compiled
nodes.summary: Compiles an expression tree into nested closures, the search's evaluator and a separate code path from interpret.

nodes.name: _differential_evolution
nodes.summary: The default global_search backend: SciPy differential evolution with integer variables and an evaluation cap.

nodes.name: register_backend
nodes.summary: Registers a named global_search backend; its answers are re-checked like any other, and the default cannot be replaced.

nodes.name: check_point
nodes.summary: Checks a search answer: point within bounds with whole integers, objective re-evaluated and compared, and optionally the projected gradient by central differences.

nodes.name: _projected_gradient
nodes.summary: Computes the projected gradient at a point by central differences, respecting box bounds.

nodes.name: lower_neighbour
nodes.summary: Probes around a local answer (gradient neighbours, axis steps, seeded random directions inside the box) for a lower point before it is called a minimum.

nodes.name: minimise
nodes.summary: Public op: multistart SciPy local search (L-BFGS-B, Nelder-Mead or Powell) on a box-bounded expression, reporting a local minimum at best, never global.

nodes.name: global_search
nodes.summary: Public op: differential evolution or a registered backend over the box, reporting the best point found after G6's re-check.

nodes.name: _starts
nodes.summary: Draws the start points for minimise: x0 first when given, the rest seeded from the box.

nodes.name: _answer
nodes.summary: Packages a checked search answer and its evidence for labelling by finish.

nodes.name: OptimisationInput
nodes.summary: Typed input for every optimisation op; fields an op does not use are ignored and fields no op has are refused.

nodes.name: OptimisationBlock
nodes.summary: AIBlock component dispatching each op to one g6.optimisation solve function and returning its labelled envelope; never verified.

nodes.name: _mathopt
nodes.summary: One OR-Tools MathOpt solve returning termination, bounds, values and, for GLOP, duals and reduced costs.

nodes.name: _no_answer
nodes.summary: Classifies a solve that ended with no answer to check, such as a time limit or unknown status.

nodes.name: _classify
nodes.summary: When GLOP finds no optimum, decides infeasible or unbounded with certificates G6 checks, else reports the solver's word uncertified.

nodes.name: _linear
nodes.summary: Solves a linear programme on GLOP and checks its optimum against the duals, or classifies a non-optimal termination.

nodes.name: _integer
nodes.summary: Solves a mixed-integer programme on SCIP and checks feasibility and objective, reporting the solver's gap.

nodes.name: _cp_sat
nodes.summary: One CP-SAT solve of a constraint model returning status, values, objective and bound.

nodes.name: _constraint
nodes.summary: Runs the CP-SAT solve for a constraint model and checks its answer before labelling.

nodes.name: solve_lp
nodes.summary: Public op: solves a linear programme on GLOP with a duality-checked optimum or a checked infeasibility or unboundedness certificate.

nodes.name: solve_mip
nodes.summary: Public op: solves a mixed-integer programme on SCIP, checked, with optimality resting on the solver's bound.

nodes.name: solve_cp
nodes.summary: Public op: solves a constraint model on CP-SAT with linear constraints, all-different groups and an optional objective.

nodes.name: Variable
nodes.summary: A decision variable with optional finite lower and upper bounds.

nodes.name: LinearConstraint
nodes.summary: A linear constraint: its terms plus optional lower and upper bounds.

nodes.name: Arc
nodes.summary: A flow network arc with endpoints, capacity and unit cost.

nodes.name: Task
nodes.summary: A job-shop task: the machine it runs on and its duration.

nodes.name: LinearProblem
nodes.summary: A linear or mixed-integer programme whose validator checks every named variable is declared and bounds are ordered.

nodes.name: CpProblem
nodes.summary: A constraint model extending LinearProblem with all-different groups and an integer-only model check.

nodes.name: KnapsackProblem
nodes.summary: A multidimensional knapsack: values, one weight list per dimension and capacities that must fit together.

nodes.name: JobShopProblem
nodes.summary: A job-shop problem: a list of jobs, each a non-empty ordered list of tasks.

nodes.name: AssignmentProblem
nodes.summary: A cost matrix for assignment, rectangular, with None marking forbidden pairs.

nodes.name: MaxFlowProblem
nodes.summary: A maximum-flow network with distinct source and sink.

nodes.name: MinCostFlowProblem
nodes.summary: A minimum-cost flow network whose node supplies must balance.

nodes.name: RoutingProblem
nodes.summary: A vehicle routing problem: distances, vehicles, depot and optional demands, capacities and time windows that must fit together.

nodes.name: OptimResult
nodes.summary: The one labelled optimisation result: objective, bound, solution, certificate, check and an envelope whose completion_state admits only qualified-draft or blocked-escalated.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Serialises request.json for one driver run: mode, nonce, limits, answers to recheck and whether the first search finished.

nodes.name: end_record
nodes.summary: Returns the driver's final end record bytes for a nonce, which the runner watches for.

nodes.name: records
nodes.summary: Extracts the driver's nonce-prefixed JSON records from output text.

nodes.name: read_output
nodes.summary: Parses and validates a whole driver run (version first, end last, only known record kinds) and refuses anything else as unrecognised output.

nodes.name: envelope.py
nodes.summary: Holds the stable G6_E_PROLOG_* codes of g6.prolog and finish(), the single place a Prolog result is labelled qualified-draft or blocked-escalated with its warning card and evidence.

nodes.name: Refusal
nodes.summary: Exception carrying a stable code and reason, raised anywhere in g6.prolog to turn a run into a blocked-escalated result.

nodes.name: labelled
nodes.summary: Runs an op's work callable, times it, and converts either its record or a Refusal into a labelled PrologResult through finish.

nodes.name: finish
nodes.summary: Builds the PrologResult envelope: decides completion_state from what SWI-Prolog ran and re-checked, attaches a blocked or amber warning card, and records the evidence.

nodes.name: _decide
nodes.summary: Decides whether a result may be qualified-draft or must carry G6_E_PROLOG_NOT_CHECKED, requiring a run and an agreeing second-process re-check for query and prove.

nodes.name: _card
nodes.summary: Writes the amber warning card for a successful op (version read, program read, goal derivable or not, answers found), including the closed-world caveat.

nodes.name: ops.py
nodes.summary: Implements the four g6.prolog ops (query, prove, check_program, swipl_version): validates limits and sizes, runs SWI-Prolog's fixed driver out of process under the restricted syntax, and re-checks every answer in a second fresh process.

nodes.name: _run_driver
nodes.summary: Writes a driver request, runs SWI-Prolog via the runner on driver.pl, and parses the driver's end-of-record output.

nodes.name: _search
nodes.summary: Locates swipl, runs the goal search, refuses programs with read problems or unsafe goals, and turns limit hits into refusals.

nodes.name: _recheck
nodes.summary: Re-runs each answer in a fresh SWI-Prolog process and, when the search finished, re-runs the search; any disagreement becomes a refusal.

nodes.name: query
nodes.summary: Public op that collects up to max_solutions answers to a goal against a program, re-checks them, and returns a labelled result.

nodes.name: prove
nodes.summary: Public op that asks whether a goal is derivable from a program (one answer), re-checked in a second process.

nodes.name: check_program
nodes.summary: Public op that has SWI-Prolog read every clause of a program without consulting it and reports its predicates or read problems.

nodes.name: swipl_version
nodes.summary: Public op that reports which SWI-Prolog executable and version would run programs, without running any program.

nodes.name: prolog_block.py
nodes.summary: PrologBlock, the registry and MCP g6_invoke door to g6.prolog, dispatching typed input to the four SWI-Prolog ops (sensitive over MCP) plus ops and help.

nodes.name: PrologInput
nodes.summary: Typed, closed input model for PrologBlock (op, program, goal, limits, request and run ids); unknown fields are refused.

nodes.name: PrologBlock
nodes.summary: Beta-maturity AIBlock whose infer routes an op to query, prove, check_program or swipl_version and returns the labelled result, never verified.

nodes.name: runner.py
nodes.summary: The only module of g6.prolog that starts a program: finds the user's swipl, writes the driver and inputs into a fresh run directory, and runs it with no start-up files under time, output and stack limits inside G6's OS boundary where available.

nodes.name: find_swipl
nodes.summary: Resolves the swipl executable from G6_SWIPL or PATH, refusing when it is missing.

nodes.name: stack_limit_mb
nodes.summary: Derives SWI-Prolog's stack limit in megabytes from the requested memory ceiling.

nodes.name: driver_arguments
nodes.summary: Builds the fixed swipl argument list (no init files, no packs, no tty, stack limit) for running driver.pl.

nodes.name: _execute
nodes.summary: Runs swipl through component_process with a time limit, an output cap and an end-of-record watcher, converting overruns and confinement failures into refusals.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Creates a confined run folder, writes the driver and caller files, plans OS confinement, executes swipl in a minimal environment, and releases the confinement.

nodes.name: version_run
nodes.summary: Returns a bounded runner that asks swipl for its version, mapping timeouts and OS errors.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Defines PrologResult, the one labelled result model of g6.prolog, whose completion_state admits only qualified-draft or blocked-escalated.

nodes.name: PrologResult
nodes.summary: Pydantic result carrying the op, SWI-Prolog version, answers, exhaustion, predicates, problems, re-check record and the cross-surface envelope fields.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Agent skill for g6-prolog with 12 sections covering when to use it, the four ops, the restricted syntax, reading results, failure modes, blind spots, requirements, examples and open problems.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the provers extension family (checking that a program or translation does what it claims); declares __g6_family__ and is not itself a component.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for g6.reasoning, re-exporting budgets, the compute-matched comparison gate, weighted voting, baseline steppers and JSON extraction for multi-call reasoning.

nodes.name: budget.py
nodes.summary: Hard ceilings on a reasoning run (model calls, output characters, wall clock) enforced by a metering wrapper around the injected LLM caller.

nodes.name: BudgetExhausted
nodes.summary: LLMError raised when a budget ceiling is reached so the caller stops and reports best-so-far or abstains.

nodes.name: Budget
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of the three ceilings, validated positive on construction.

nodes.name: MeteredCaller
nodes.summary: LLM caller wrapper that counts every call and its output, checks elapsed time, and raises BudgetExhausted before or after a call breaches a ceiling.

nodes.name: compare.py
nodes.summary: A paired baseline gate that promotes a candidate reasoning method only with at least 30 cases, an exact one-sided sign test, a margin, and no extra model calls.

nodes.name: Case
nodes.summary: One comparison case: a problem and the scoring function applied to an arm's answer.

nodes.name: Arm
nodes.summary: A named method under comparison whose run returns an answer and the model calls it used.

nodes.name: Verdict
nodes.summary: Outcome of a comparison: promoted flag, reason, win/loss/tie counts, p-value, mean scores, call counts, compute-matching and failures.

nodes.name: sign_test_p
nodes.summary: Computes the one-sided exact binomial sign-test p-value for wins over losses.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Runs baseline and candidate on every case, clips scores, tallies wins and losses, and returns a Verdict that promotes only on significance, margin and matched compute.

nodes.name: metrics.py
nodes.summary: Classification and regression metrics with explicit direction and thresholds plus a Clopper-Pearson style exact interval; invalid inputs raise instead of scoring as zero loss.

nodes.name: _number
nodes.summary: Coerces a value to a finite float, rejecting booleans, non-numbers and non-finite values.

nodes.name: score
nodes.summary: Computes a named metric (accuracy, exact match, macro/micro/weighted precision-recall-F1, MSE, MAE, RMSE) over paired predictions and truth.

nodes.name: exact_interval
nodes.summary: Computes an exact binomial confidence interval for a success count by bisection on the binomial tail.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Scores predictions against several metric thresholds and reports which pass according to each metric's direction.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Agent skill for g6-reasoning with 11 sections on budgets, weighted voting, baselines and the compute-matched comparison gate, including its Python API, failure modes and blind spots.

nodes.name: steps.py
nodes.summary: Baseline reasoning steppers (one direct call and n-call self-consistency) and LaTeX-safe extraction of the first JSON object from model output.

nodes.name: _escape_lone_backslashes
nodes.summary: Escapes lone backslashes inside JSON strings so LaTeX commands survive json parsing while real escapes stay intact.

nodes.name: first_json_object
nodes.summary: Scans model output for the first balanced JSON object and parses it, retrying with LaTeX-safe escaping.

nodes.name: DirectStep
nodes.summary: Single-call baseline that asks the injected model once and parses its answer.

nodes.name: self_consistency
nodes.summary: N-call baseline that samples several answers and combines them with weighted_vote.

nodes.name: structure.py
nodes.summary: Compares small labelled directed graphs (up to seven nodes) for structural correspondence with networkx VF2 (an optional extra), matching labels exactly and never by name similarity.

nodes.name: _validate
nodes.summary: Validates a graph spec has only nodes and well-formed labelled edges between known nodes.

nodes.name: structure_map
nodes.summary: Returns the largest induced labelled mapping between two graphs of at most seven nodes using networkx VF2, answering a blocked-escalated envelope for invalid input or a missing networkx.

nodes.name: vote.py
nodes.summary: Pure weighted voting over candidate answers in which checked answers dominate, reporting whether a real majority exists rather than a bare plurality.

nodes.name: normalise
nodes.summary: Lower-cases, collapses whitespace and strips trailing punctuation so equivalent answers vote together.

nodes.name: Candidate
nodes.summary: Frozen candidate answer with its weight and a flag set only when an independent check accepted it.

nodes.name: VoteResult
nodes.summary: Vote outcome with the winner, its weight, total, answer groups, abstained weight and whether the winner holds a strict majority.

nodes.name: weighted_vote
nodes.summary: Groups equivalent candidates, counts only independently checked ones when any exist, treats empty answers as abstentions against a majority, and reports the winner and whether it holds a strict majority.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package entry for the intake slice of the reliability pipeline, documenting its limits and lazily exposing stages, intake, failure-mode skills, the premortem constructor, the feasibility assessor and metacognition's experience recall via __getattr__.

nodes.name: failure_modes.py
nodes.summary: Pure-data catalogue of curated, unmeasured failure-mode skills, including the nonadjacent event-replay requirement and its single supported phrasing, with a relevance matcher.

nodes.name: states_replay_requirement
nodes.summary: Checks whether text states the supported phrasing of the nonadjacent replay requirement.

nodes.name: Interpretation
nodes.summary: One candidate reading of an ambiguous requirement within a failure-mode skill.

nodes.name: FailureModeSkill
nodes.summary: Frozen record of a curated failure mode: its triggers, question, interpretations and guidance, granting no execution authority.

nodes.name: relevant
nodes.summary: Returns the failure-mode skills whose triggers match an objective.

nodes.name: feasibility.py
nodes.summary: Rule-based feasibility triage for intake: structural blocks for missing success criteria or context, plus word-boundary tripwire signals that mark goals risky, too large or underspecified without ever hard-blocking alone.

nodes.name: ReportAssumption
nodes.summary: An assumption a feasibility report rests on and whether it was checked.

nodes.name: FeasibilityReport
nodes.summary: Feasibility verdict with signals, assumptions and the recommended next step.

nodes.name: recommended_next_step
nodes.summary: Maps a feasibility status to the next step a caller should take.

nodes.name: FeasibilityClassificationDecision
nodes.summary: Intermediate classification decision holding status, signals and reasons before a report is built.

nodes.name: classified_text
nodes.summary: Joins the objective and criteria text that the tripwire classification scans.

nodes.name: _matches
nodes.summary: Finds word-boundary tripwire phrases in text, cancelling those directly preceded by a negation.

nodes.name: names_context
nodes.summary: Detects whether a request refers to context (an attached document, a file) it does not carry.

nodes.name: _unchecked
nodes.summary: Lists the assumptions a rule-based verdict leaves unchecked.

nodes.name: deterministic_classify
nodes.summary: Applies the structural blocks and tripwire signals to produce a feasibility classification decision.

nodes.name: report_from_decision
nodes.summary: Builds a FeasibilityReport from a classification decision, attaching assumptions and the next step.

nodes.name: deterministic_assess
nodes.summary: Runs the rule-based classification and returns its report.

nodes.name: at_least
nodes.summary: Merges an injected assessor's report with the rule floor so an assessor can only tighten, never relax, the verdict.

nodes.name: FeasibilityAssessor
nodes.summary: Rule-based feasibility assessor used by intake by default, wrapping deterministic_assess behind an assess method.

nodes.name: intake.py
nodes.summary: Stage 0 task intake: extracts SMART acceptance criteria, derives escalation triggers, asks the replay question, runs feasibility triage and returns a StageResult with an IntakeContract.

nodes.name: IntakeContract
nodes.summary: The contract intake produces: objective, acceptance criteria, escalation triggers, feasibility and clarification questions.

nodes.name: replay_question
nodes.summary: Builds the clarification question asked first when an objective concerns retries, duplicates or idempotency.

nodes.name: _extract_acceptance_criteria
nodes.summary: Pulls acceptance criteria from a request, dropping filler and placeholder entries.

nodes.name: derive_escalation_triggers
nodes.summary: Derives the conditions under which work must escalate to a person from the objective and feasibility signals.

nodes.name: _clarification_default_on
nodes.summary: Reads the environment switch that decides whether clarification questions are on by default.

nodes.name: run_intake
nodes.summary: Runs stage 0 end to end: criteria extraction, feasibility assessment (injected or rule-based), risk holds, escalation triggers and clarification, returning an advanced, downgraded or blocked StageResult.

nodes.name: metacognition.py
nodes.summary: Optional experience recall across runs: distills a finished run into a store the caller passes and hands back experiences for the same task signature, each cited by a run the store knows, with no confidence reported.

nodes.name: Experience
nodes.summary: Stored record of a run's task signature, trace, outcome, reward and run id.

nodes.name: ExperienceStore
nodes.summary: Protocol a caller's store implements: has_run, add and similar.

nodes.name: distill_run
nodes.summary: Stores what a finished run did, but only for a run the store knows.

nodes.name: reconsume
nodes.summary: Returns stored experiences matching a task signature, dropping any whose cited run the store does not know.

nodes.name: plan.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic plan critique: a structural check for goal, criteria, tests and rollback, a lexical tripwire for risky wording, and a merge that keeps the strictest verdict as a reliability envelope.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.summary: A plan's goal, acceptance criteria, tests, rollback and steps.

nodes.name: CritiqueFinding
nodes.summary: One critique finding with its category, severity and message.

nodes.name: CritiqueReport
nodes.summary: Critique verdict and findings, mapping a pass to at best qualified-draft and serialising to a reliability envelope.

nodes.name: stricter_verdict
nodes.summary: Returns the stricter of two critique verdicts.

nodes.name: severity_verdict
nodes.summary: Derives a verdict from the most severe finding.

nodes.name: critique_structure
nodes.summary: Flags a plan whose goal, criteria, tests or rollback is missing or only a placeholder.

nodes.name: lexical_tripwire
nodes.summary: Scans plan text for risky or hand-waving wording and asks for revision without blocking.

nodes.name: merge_reports
nodes.summary: Unites findings by category and keeps the strictest verdict across the floor report and another report.

nodes.name: critique
nodes.summary: Runs the structural check and tripwire on a plan and merges an optional extra report.

nodes.name: premortem.py
nodes.summary: Stage 1 premortem: the constant failure-mode checklist and construct_replay_check, a narrow regex-bounded constructor that builds a task-derived, nonindependent replay check for one benchmark phrasing of an event-replay requirement.

nodes.name: constructor
nodes.summary: Returns the identity and limits of the replay-check constructor that every construction reports.

nodes.name: construct_replay_check
nodes.summary: Recognises the supported replay requirement and builds a bounded test that can refute, never independently support, a change, stating its template limits.

nodes.name: premortem_failure_mode_questions
nodes.summary: Returns the thirteen premortem failure-mode questions.

nodes.name: hypotheses
nodes.summary: Returns the competing ways a task can fail, unranked: the coding hypotheses (each with the check that would test it) followed by the premortem checklist.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Agent skill for g6-reliability-pipeline with 10 sections on intake, feasibility triage, the thirteen-question premortem, plan critique and the replay-check constructor, including its Python API and blind spots.

nodes.name: stages.py
nodes.summary: Stage primitives for the reliability state machine: the Stage enum, stage states and StageResult with advance, downgrade and block transitions carrying an evidence bundle.

nodes.name: Stage
nodes.summary: String enum naming the reliability pipeline stages from stage 0 intake through premortem, risk tiering, plan and budget, routing, execution, checking and handoff to stage 8 learning.

nodes.name: StageState
nodes.summary: String enum of a stage's outcome: advance, downgrade or block.

nodes.name: StageResult
nodes.summary: Frozen result of a stage with its state, reason, safe next action, optional evidence bundle and metadata, built through the advance, downgrade or block class methods.

nodes.name: task_contract.py
nodes.summary: TaskContract v1 value types: task modes, success criteria with their checkers, and the cap reasons and human-checker audit that decide whether an output may be labelled verified as fit for purpose.

nodes.name: TaskMode
nodes.summary: Enum of how a deliverable is judged: evidentiary (full checking, may reach verified) or exploratory (capped at qualified-draft).

nodes.name: coerce_task_mode
nodes.summary: Coerces a string or enum value to a TaskMode, rejecting unknown modes.

nodes.name: SuccessCriterion
nodes.summary: A task success criterion with criticality and checking method, reporting whether a checker is available for it.

nodes.name: _coerce_one
nodes.summary: Coerces one criterion given as a string, mapping or SuccessCriterion into a SuccessCriterion.

nodes.name: derive_criteria
nodes.summary: Derives the task's success criteria from supplied criteria and the task mode.

nodes.name: task_contract_cap_reasons
nodes.summary: Lists the reasons a result must be capped below verified because critical criteria lack an available or passing checker.

nodes.name: task_contract_human_verifier_audit
nodes.summary: Audits criteria that rely on a human checker and records what a person must still confirm.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for G6 research programmes (CSIR, RVC, ECHA, AHI), stating that every module beneath it is at most at the "implemented" maturity level and pointing to docs/theory for the specifications.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel for AHI governed harness adaptation: re-exports failure-case, proposal, control, funnel and learned-component contracts plus the local-validation and promotion-gate wrappers. Research code that is off by default behind G6_ECHA_RESEARCH.

nodes.name: contracts.py
nodes.summary: Typed dataclass contracts from the ECHA spec sections 4.4-4.5 for governed adaptation: a FailureCase with a root-cause taxonomy, a LearnedComponent descriptor and a Funnel tracking present-reachable-activated-effective stages; AdaptationProposal and Control are re-exported from the product adaptation gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses validate required fields in __post_init__, so a malformed contract cannot be constructed.

nodes.name: FailureCase
nodes.summary: Dataclass for a real failure that motivates an adaptation; refuses a root cause outside the spec taxonomy and requires a reproducible case and alternative explanations.

nodes.name: LearnedComponent
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a learned harness component with version, implementation hash, activation trigger, rollback target, permissions and contraindications; validates its id and 64-hex implementation hash.

nodes.name: Funnel
nodes.summary: Records a component moving through the present, reachable, activated and effective stages in order; the effective stage demands a counterfactual evidence reference rather than an invocation log.

nodes.name: flag.py
nodes.summary: Research flag for AHI: governed adaptation stays off unless G6_ECHA_RESEARCH holds a plain yes, and every AHI entry point raises ResearchDisabled otherwise.

nodes.name: ResearchDisabled
nodes.summary: RuntimeError raised when AHI research code is called while its flag is off, signalling that nothing was created, written or read.

nodes.name: research_enabled
nodes.summary: Returns true only when the G6_ECHA_RESEARCH variable is a plain yes (1, true, yes, on); anything else, including a typo, reads as off and it never raises.

nodes.name: require_research
nodes.summary: Guard that raises ResearchDisabled unless the AHI research flag is on.

nodes.name: lifecycle.py
nodes.summary: Flag-gated wrappers over the product adaptation gate for ECHA phase C (local validation against controls) and phase E (promotion decision), whose best outcome is shadow approval.

nodes.name: validate_locally
nodes.summary: Checks the research flag, then runs a candidate guard on every control through g6.core.adaptation_gate.validate_locally.

nodes.name: decide_promotion
nodes.summary: Checks the research flag, then delegates to the product promotion gate, which blocks on unknowns, rejects on failure and grants isolated shadow use at most.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel for ECHA, an audit and analysis view over the issuer's records: re-exports the access boundary, claim rule, episodes, ledger, typed records, trace and certificate view. It is explicitly not a second authority on requirement status.

nodes.name: access.py
nodes.summary: Names the product vault (g6.core.vault) as ECHA's evaluator-only access boundary for hidden tests and oracles; documents that this is an in-process software check, not an operating-system boundary, so dependent results are marked unblinded.

nodes.name: adapters.py
nodes.summary: Conservative adapters from workforce mechanism and elicitation records (plain dicts) into ECHA EvidenceRecords, mapping a check to unknown, partial falsifier, heuristic review or independent executable.

nodes.name: evidence_from_mechanism_record
nodes.summary: Builds an EvidenceRecord from one workforce mechanism record, classifying its evidence category conservatively and attaching standard, oracle, fixture and scope metadata.

nodes.name: known_unknowns
nodes.summary: Extracts the known unknowns listed in a verify cycle's failure elicitation record.

nodes.name: claims.py
nodes.summary: The ECHA claim rule: computes a claim's result (supported, refuted or inconclusive with reasons) from its ledgered evidence, requiring an active check with a failed negative control, treating reviews as leads, binding evidence to the subject's bytes and adding oracle error bounds.

nodes.name: subject_artefact
nodes.summary: Parses the sha256 artefact digest a claim's subject names, if any.

nodes.name: _control_holds
nodes.summary: Decides whether a check is active by finding a recorded negative control by the same evaluator that failed on the same standard and predicate, outside contaminated fixtures.

nodes.name: evaluate_claim
nodes.summary: Evaluates a ledgered claim against all its cited evidence, sorting records into active support, structural protections, leads and refutations, applying subject binding and error-bound rules, and returning the verdict with reasons.

nodes.name: competence.py
nodes.summary: Research-only competence analysis over ECHA episodes: a Beta-posterior lower bound on a task family's success rate from admissible episodes, autonomy advice against a frozen policy, a success-claim consistency check and owner-scoped similar-episode retrieval. Retired for selection.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the regularised incomplete Beta function with a continued fraction (math.lgamma) and bisection for the credible lower bound, avoiding a SciPy dependency.

nodes.name: CompetencePolicy
nodes.summary: Frozen policy for competence advice: threshold, minimum episodes, margin, credible level and admissible oracles, with validation and a stable digest.

nodes.name: CompetenceEstimate
nodes.summary: Result of a competence computation: successes, failures, excluded counts by reason, Beta lower bound, mean and the policy digest.

nodes.name: Advice
nodes.summary: Autonomy advice record (grant flag, reason, policy digest); advisory only and never a completion state.

nodes.name: ConsistencyVerdict
nodes.summary: Result of a success-claim consistency check: a consistency flag and the problems found.

nodes.name: ScoredEpisode
nodes.summary: A retrieved episode with its score, score scale and the retriever backend named.

nodes.name: _betacf
nodes.summary: Continued-fraction evaluation used by the regularised incomplete Beta function.

nodes.name: _exclusion
nodes.summary: Returns the reason an episode is inadmissible for a task family and policy (broken body, dependent or unadmitted oracle, non-decisive outcome), or none.

nodes.name: competence
nodes.summary: Counts admissible successes and failures for a task family and returns a CompetenceEstimate with the Beta lower bound and exclusion counts.

nodes.name: autonomy_advice
nodes.summary: Advises granting or refusing autonomy by comparing the estimate's episode count and lower bound against the policy threshold and margin.

nodes.name: success_claim_consistent
nodes.summary: Internal-consistency pre-check on an episode claiming success: intact body, outcome events and evidence references agree.

nodes.name: similar_episodes
nodes.summary: Owner-scoped top-k retrieval over case texts through a caller-supplied retriever with a score floor and outcome filter, naming the backend and refusing pseudo-embedding fallbacks.

nodes.name: custody.py
nodes.summary: Bounded custody helpers for ECHA records: reads what a record is about and which evaluator it names through the product mapping's binding reader, and decodes a raw artefact into checked evidence under size and strict-JSON limits.

nodes.name: binding_of
nodes.summary: Returns the custody binding held in a record's source_ref, read through g6.evidence.mapping.read_binding.

nodes.name: about
nodes.summary: Returns what a record is about (artefact, standard, predicate) from its binding when present, else its own fields, via the mapping's single reader.

nodes.name: receipt_about
nodes.summary: Reads what an issuer receipt is about, preferring the custody binding in its provenance and refusing an unreadable one.

nodes.name: evaluator_of
nodes.summary: Returns the evaluator a record names, compared by bytes through its binding digest, so a declared label never matches a byte-named evaluator.

nodes.name: _decode
nodes.summary: Decodes raw bytes as strict JSON object under a size limit, raising on anything else.

nodes.name: decode_artifact
nodes.summary: Public strict decoder for a raw research artefact.

nodes.name: checked_evidence
nodes.summary: Turns a decoded artefact into a partial-falsifier EvidenceRecord after checking its binding matches the expected standard, predicate and purpose.

nodes.name: episodes.py
nodes.summary: Append-only, hash-chained episode records (ECHA spec 4.2): events carry only ids, hashes, codes and counts, a forecast must precede the outcome and cannot be backfilled, and the outcome is one of the existing wire states.

nodes.name: _detail
nodes.summary: Validates an event detail mapping holds only scalars or short scalar lists, refusing free text payloads.

nodes.name: verify_episode_body
nodes.summary: Recomputes an episode body's hash chain and checks event order, forecast-before-outcome, outcome agreement and builder rules, returning every problem found.

nodes.name: _builder_rules
nodes.summary: Checks the builder invariants of a stored episode: header fields, finite cost and latency, artefact hash, single outcome, forecast order and event detail shape.

nodes.name: EpisodeRecord
nodes.summary: Frozen record of a completed episode (header, genesis, events, head hash, outcome, evidence refs, cost, latency) with accessors and to_dict.

nodes.name: Episode
nodes.summary: Builder for an episode: validates its header, appends hash-chained events under ordering rules, and freezes into an EpisodeRecord with outcome, cost and latency checks.

nodes.name: example.py
nodes.summary: Synthetic end-to-end ECHA evidence trace runnable as a module: writes a ledger with one supported claim (differential probe with a negative control), one inconclusive claim (reviews by one model family) and a check that cannot fail.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Populates a ledger with a standard, vault, evidence records (including one adapted from a mechanism record), an episode and two claims to illustrate supported and inconclusive outcomes.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that builds the example ledger at the given path and prints each claim's evaluation and trace as JSON.

nodes.name: ledger.py
nodes.summary: ECHA evidence ledger layered on the product hash chain (g6.core.ledger): enforces readable custody bindings, known standards, same-evaluator failed negative controls, existing cited evidence and intact episode bodies, and audits the chain against a kept head.

nodes.name: _semantic
nodes.summary: Checks the semantic references of each ledger entry kind: evidence binding readability, standard presence and negative-control validity, claim evidence presence and episode body integrity.

nodes.name: Ledger
nodes.summary: Append-only ECHA ledger with typed add methods for standards, evidence, claims, episodes, vaults and incidents, lookup accessors, full verification, head-anchored audit and contaminated-fixture listing.

nodes.name: records.py
nodes.summary: ECHA kernel value objects: StandardRef, EvidenceRecord and ClaimRecord, each validated on construction and hashed as canonical JSON, plus canonicalisation, digest and text-validation helpers shared across the research packages.

nodes.name: canonical
nodes.summary: Serialises a value as canonical sorted-key compact JSON.

nodes.name: digest
nodes.summary: SHA-256 hex digest of a value's canonical JSON.

nodes.name: text_of
nodes.summary: Validates and returns a required non-empty, bounded text field.

nodes.name: texts_of
nodes.summary: Validates and returns a tuple of bounded text values.

nodes.name: hex64_of
nodes.summary: Validates that a value is a 64-character lowercase hex digest.

nodes.name: StandardRef
nodes.summary: Reference to a frozen standard (id, version, predicates, sha256) with construction from text and dict round-tripping.

nodes.name: EvidenceRecord
nodes.summary: Typed evidence record carrying category, predicate, result, scope, provenance, oracle and fixture versions, independence group, negative control and limits; unknown is never a pass and non-discriminating evidence is neither pass nor fail.

nodes.name: ClaimRecord
nodes.summary: Typed claim record naming subject, standard, predicate, scope and cited evidence, with no result field because its result is computed by the claim rule.

nodes.name: trace.py
nodes.summary: Traces an ECHA claim to its exact standard, evidence with negative controls, episodes that used the evidence, computed verdict and the ledger's chain and reference integrity.

nodes.name: trace_claim
nodes.summary: Builds a trace dict for a claim: standard, each evidence record with body-hash check and negative control, linked episodes, the evaluate_claim verdict and ledger verification status.

nodes.name: view.py
nodes.summary: ECHA certificate view: explains an issuer certificate (from g6.evidence.certificate) per predicate without recomputing any status, showing each receipt's role, ledger presence, scope and environment, and refusing a certificate for other bytes than the subject.

nodes.name: _bound
nodes.summary: Determines whether a receipt is bound to the subject's bytes using its custody binding or own artefact.

nodes.name: certificate_view
nodes.summary: Public entry that refuses a certificate whose subject bytes differ and otherwise builds the per-predicate explanatory view.

nodes.name: _view
nodes.summary: Assembles the view body: per predicate the issuer status copied as given, plus each receipt's role, ledger resolution, provenance, scope and environment.

nodes.name: source_record
nodes.summary: Describes an ECHA record as a source, marking that ECHA records are never a source of evidence for the issuer.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel for the mission bridge research package: a mission as a typed graph (MissionIR) and the pre-run screen for type mismatches, missing prerequisites, unauthorised ops, lowered standards, unapproved egress and budget overruns. Off unless G6_MISSION_BRIDGE=1.

nodes.name: bundle.py
nodes.summary: Claim and evidence bundle for a mission: types each node observation (process, model opinion, executable, formal) into an ECHA evidence category, writes it to the kernel ledger, derives claim results with the ECHA claim rule and yields qualified-draft or blocked-escalated, never verified.

nodes.name: BundleRefused
nodes.summary: Error raised with the list of reasons a bundle cannot be built.

nodes.name: Observation
nodes.summary: What a mission node actually produced, typed by evidence kind, with optional negative control and formal certificate; validated on construction.

nodes.name: ClaimSpec
nodes.summary: Specification of a claim to derive: predicate, scope, subject and the observations it rests on.

nodes.name: Outcome
nodes.summary: Per-claim outcome in the bundle: result, reasons and gate decision.

nodes.name: Bundle
nodes.summary: Final bundle: completion state, claim outcomes, unknowns, rejected observations and the ledger head, with an evidence-category summary.

nodes.name: standard_ref
nodes.summary: Builds an ECHA StandardRef for a mission's frozen standard.

nodes.name: _record
nodes.summary: Maps one observation to an EvidenceRecord in the correct category, rejecting a formal claim without a valid certificate from a formal op the graph names.

nodes.name: _refusals
nodes.summary: Collects every reason the inputs cannot form a bundle: unknown nodes, missing predicates, observation and claim inconsistencies.

nodes.name: _outcome
nodes.summary: Combines a claim's evaluated result with the person-gate decision, which completes but never supplies support.

nodes.name: build_bundle
nodes.summary: Flag-gated entry that validates inputs, writes observations and claims into a fresh ECHA ledger, evaluates each claim and returns the Bundle with its completion state.

nodes.name: checks.py
nodes.summary: Pure mission-graph validator: reads a MissionIR against an op catalogue and reports every problem as a Finding with a stable code covering graph shape, authority, standard lowering, egress approval, budget and roles; it runs and approves nothing.

nodes.name: OpFact
nodes.summary: Catalogue fact for a component op: declared side effect and authority class, validated on construction.

nodes.name: Finding
nodes.summary: A validator finding with a stable code, node and message.

nodes.name: _graph
nodes.summary: Checks graph shape: unknown ops, type mismatches between providers and requirements, missing prerequisites and cycles via graphlib TopologicalSorter.

nodes.name: _authority
nodes.summary: Flags nodes whose authority class is below what their declared effect requires.

nodes.name: _standard
nodes.summary: Flags nodes that drop or lower predicates of the mission's frozen standard.

nodes.name: _egress
nodes.summary: Flags nodes that send data out without an approval.

nodes.name: _roles
nodes.summary: Flags required roles left unfilled.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Flag-gated entry that runs every graph, authority, standard, egress, budget and role check and returns all findings sorted.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package docstring for the CSIR kernel of the Runtime Validator Constructor: the typing judgement with obligations A1-A6, standard refinement, Belnap evidence certificates and an advisory solvability belief. Research code behind G6_MISSION_BRIDGE.

nodes.name: certificate.py
nodes.summary: Research rig adapter to the product certificate issuer (g6.evidence.certificate): judges a MissionIR with the CSIR judgement, binds it to the frozen standard and hands MissionFacts to the issuer for issue and verification.

nodes.name: facts_of
nodes.summary: Builds MissionFacts for the issuer from a MissionIR, catalogue and frozen standard, including the judgement result and catalogue hash.

nodes.name: issue
nodes.summary: Flag-gated wrapper that issues a certificate for a mission through the product issuer.

nodes.name: verify
nodes.summary: Re-checks an issued certificate against the mission facts through the product verifier.

nodes.name: judgement.py
nodes.summary: CSIR typing judgement over a MissionIR: files every validator finding under the soundness obligation A1-A6 it breaks (refinement, composition, authority, budget, evidence authority, hidden shared state) and computes composed resources, so a mission is sound only when none is broken.
nodes.languageNotes: Encodes a typing judgement and a conditional soundness theorem as executable checks over a DAG.

nodes.name: Resources
nodes.summary: Resource bound of a program (cost, effects) with composition that keeps unknown costs unknown.

nodes.name: Judgement
nodes.summary: Result of the typing judgement: findings by obligation, resources and the sound property.

nodes.name: _ancestors
nodes.summary: Computes each node's ancestor set in the mission DAG for ordering checks.

nodes.name: judge
nodes.summary: Flag-gated entry that runs the validator, adds the parallel-writer A6 check, maps findings to obligations and returns the Judgement.

nodes.name: solvability.py
nodes.summary: Advisory solvability belief on three independent axes (existence, findability, optimality) that never gates an attempt or changes a completion state.

nodes.name: Solvability
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding existence, findability and optimality beliefs with bases; validates axis values, always permits an attempt and renders a description and dict.

nodes.name: standard.py
nodes.summary: Standard refinement S' >= S for frozen standards: a standard changes only by a re-freeze that adds predicates with a stated reason and names its parent hash, and a revision chain can be checked offline.

nodes.name: NotARefinement
nodes.summary: ValueError raised when a proposed standard revision drops a predicate or is otherwise not a refinement.

nodes.name: FrozenStandard
nodes.summary: Immutable standard revision with predicates, reason and parent hash, built by first() and hashed by sha256().

nodes.name: refines
nodes.summary: True when every mandatory predicate of the old standard stays in the new one.

nodes.name: refreeze
nodes.summary: Creates a child FrozenStandard that adds at least one predicate with a reason, linking to its parent hash.

nodes.name: chain_problems
nodes.summary: Checks a revision chain offline, reporting dropped predicates and broken parent links.

nodes.name: fixtures.py
nodes.summary: Loads the mission-bridge synthetic fixtures (medico-legal, engineering and coding mission graphs, their recordings, the frozen standards and the replay catalogue) from the fixtures/ JSON folder, returning a fresh dict per call.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Returns one named mission graph fixture (medico_legal, engineering or coding) as a fresh dict, refusing unknown names.

nodes.name: recording
nodes.summary: Returns the synthetic recording (placeholder inputs, decisions and outputs) for one named mission fixture.

nodes.name: standard_body
nodes.summary: Returns the frozen standard text, provenance and predicates for one named mission domain from standards.json.

nodes.name: replay_record
nodes.summary: Reads the replay catalogue JSON describing each operation the fixtures name and its assumed or census class.

nodes.name: replay_catalogue
nodes.summary: Converts the replay catalogue record into OpFact entries keyed by operation name for the mission checks.

nodes.name: coding.json
nodes.summary: Synthetic coding-change mission graph (mission_ir.v1 shape): task, repository and patch inputs, a frozen coding standard with test predicates, and work/verify nodes naming real G6 operations with effects, data classes and budgets.

nodes.name: coding.recording.json
nodes.summary: Synthetic placeholder recording for the coding mission: inputs, recorded gate decisions and per-node outputs used by replay; nothing in it was run.

nodes.name: engineering.json
nodes.summary: Synthetic engineering mission graph from the audit illustration, with scope, standards, calculation, geometry and supply nodes plus verify units, approvals and required roles; it deliberately omits a design load.

nodes.name: engineering.recording.json
nodes.summary: Synthetic placeholder recording for the engineering mission, including the design_load input, standards-approval and engineer-review decisions, and node outputs for replay.

nodes.name: medico_legal.json
nodes.summary: Synthetic medico-legal mission graph from the audit illustration, with source-linked evidence, image interpretation, privacy and expert sign-off nodes, egress approvals and required roles.

nodes.name: medico_legal.recording.json
nodes.summary: Synthetic placeholder recording for the medico-legal mission: inputs, recorded decisions and node outputs for replay; no value is a result.

nodes.name: replay_catalogue.json
nodes.summary: Catalogue of every operation the fixtures name, with its effect, authority class and whether the class comes from the shipped census or is an assumption the experiment makes, pinned to a census build and digest.

nodes.name: standards.json
nodes.summary: Frozen standards for the three synthetic mission domains (medico-legal, engineering, coding), each with an id, text, provenance and its list of acceptance predicates.

nodes.name: flag.py
nodes.summary: The mission-bridge research flag: the research code stays off unless G6_MISSION_BRIDGE holds a plain yes, and every entry point refuses with ResearchDisabled otherwise.

nodes.name: ResearchDisabled
nodes.summary: RuntimeError raised when the mission-bridge research flag is off, so nothing was built or judged.

nodes.name: research_enabled
nodes.summary: Returns True only when the flag variable in the given mapping or the environment is a plain yes; never raises.

nodes.name: require_research
nodes.summary: Raises ResearchDisabled with setup guidance unless the mission-bridge research flag is on.

nodes.name: ir.py
nodes.summary: Defines the research MissionIR: a mission graph as typed, hashed, immutable records (standards, nodes, approvals) read strictly from a document, refusing unknown fields or bad values with every problem listed.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses plus precompiled regular expressions give a strict, non-repairing parser that accumulates every problem before raising.

nodes.name: IRRejected
nodes.summary: ValueError carrying every problem found in a mission document the bridge refuses to read.

nodes.name: Standard
nodes.summary: Frozen record of the mission frozen standard: its id, sha256 hash and predicates.

nodes.name: NodeStandard
nodes.summary: Frozen record of a node-level standard reference: the standard hash and predicates a verify node checks.

nodes.name: Approval
nodes.summary: Frozen record of a recorded approval for a node and its scope (egress or egress_sensitive).

nodes.name: Node
nodes.summary: Frozen mission graph node: role, source operation, declared effect, typed requires/provides, data class, egress, budget, verify target, standard and gate; exposes its component name.

nodes.name: MissionIR
nodes.summary: The whole mission graph as an immutable record with canonical dict form, a sha256 over its JSON, and from_dict which requires the research flag and parses strictly.

nodes.name: _fields
nodes.summary: Checks a raw mapping for unknown and missing keys against allowed and required sets, recording each problem.

nodes.name: _node
nodes.summary: Parses one raw node entry into a Node, validating its id, operation pattern, effect, data class, egress, typed artifacts, standard and budget.

nodes.name: _read
nodes.summary: Parses a whole mission document into a MissionIR, validating the standard, unique node ids, approvals, roles and budget fields.

nodes.name: replay.py
nodes.summary: Replays a mission graph over recorded values in dependency order without running any operation, producing a trace of replayed, decided, blocked or waiting steps and the names nothing provides.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses graphlib.TopologicalSorter for dependency order and reports a CycleError as a refusal.

nodes.name: Step
nodes.summary: Frozen record of one replayed node: its source operation, declared effect, gate, status and what it still needs.

nodes.name: Trace
nodes.summary: Frozen replay result: the ordered steps, the names asked for that nothing supplies, and the operations replayed.

nodes.name: _check_names
nodes.summary: Refuses replay inputs, decisions or recordings that name nodes or inputs the graph does not declare.

nodes.name: replay
nodes.summary: Walks the mission graph in topological order, taking recorded outputs where requirements are met, stopping on missing or mismatched recordings and waiting at gates without a recorded decision.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package entry for g6.safety_engine, the trusted per-run ceilings and pre-action check; re-exports the static test-weakening check and declares the component metadata (beta, mitigates runaway_run and test_weakening).

nodes.name: ceilings.py
nodes.summary: Projects one proposed action against every runtime ceiling (tool calls, steps, shell commands, files, lines, runtime, privilege, cost) and names the first it would breach.

nodes.name: exceeds_ceiling
nodes.summary: Returns the first ceiling an action would breach given the run state counters and the policy, or None when all hold.

nodes.name: kill_switch.py
nodes.summary: A run-scoped, thread-safe kill switch that trips one way and can be reset only with the token minted at creation, compared by digest in constant time.

nodes.name: KillSwitch
nodes.summary: One-way run stop with a lock; with_reset_token returns a switch and its sole reset token, and reset refuses a wrong token with PermissionError.

nodes.name: policy_engine.py
nodes.summary: The pre-action decision: checks kill switch and process stop, ceilings, guard verdicts, validator quorum, allow-list, forbidden paths and tests-before-final, returning ALLOW, BLOCK or ESCALATE without minting any token.

nodes.name: PolicyEngine
nodes.summary: Authorizes or refuses one action at a time against trusted policy, counting each decision as a run step and tripping the kill switch on a guard BLOCK.

nodes.name: quorum.py
nodes.summary: Counts declared validator votes by distinct fault domain and decides whether a policy quorum (n, f, required accepts) is met; it proves nothing about independence.

nodes.name: bft_shape_ok
nodes.summary: True when the policy quorum settings satisfy the BFT relations n = 3f + 1 and required accepts = 2f + 1.

nodes.name: count_independent_accepts
nodes.summary: Counts approving fault domains, excluding any domain that also cast a rejecting vote.

nodes.name: quorum_satisfied
nodes.summary: Returns whether the votes clear the policy quorum: a pass-through when quorum is off, failing closed when the BFT shape is wrong.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Frozen data types of the safety engine: the trusted RuntimePolicy, the untrusted ActionRequest, guard verdicts, validator votes and the AuthorizationDecision.

nodes.name: RuntimePolicy
nodes.summary: Frozen trusted ceilings for one run: steps, tool calls, shell commands, files, lines, retries, runtime, cost, privilege, allow-list, forbidden paths, tests-before-final and quorum settings.

nodes.name: ActionRequest
nodes.summary: One proposed tool call as untrusted data: tool, arguments, reason, files touched, privilege, shell flag, estimated lines, cost ceiling and is_final.

nodes.name: GuardVerdict
nodes.summary: A guard scanner verdict passed into authorization: decision, reason, matched patterns, risk score, evidence and surface.

nodes.name: ValidatorVote
nodes.summary: One validator vote with its declared fault domain, decision, reason and evidence.

nodes.name: AuthorizationDecision
nodes.summary: The pre-action decision: ALLOW, BLOCK or ESCALATE with reason, permitted action, policy checks run, guard verdicts and votes.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Agent skill guide for the G6 safety engine with 11 sections: when to use and not use it, the Python API, reading results, composition, failure modes caught, blind spots, needs, examples and four open problems.

nodes.name: state.py
nodes.summary: RunState: the mutable per-run counters (steps, tool calls, shell commands, files, lines, retries, cost, tests) with the run kill switch and policy, plus projections used by ceiling checks.

nodes.name: RunState
nodes.summary: Per-run counters and projections (steps_after, cost_after, elapsed_seconds and similar) with record_* methods for executions, steps, retries, tests and cost.

nodes.name: weakening.py
nodes.summary: Static before/after comparison of test files, conftest.py, startup customisation files and pytest/CI configuration to detect whether a change weakened the tests; runs nothing and never reports verified.
nodes.languageNotes: Parses Python with the ast module, pytest settings with configparser and tomllib, and compares extracted facts (tests, checks, markers, patches) rather than raw text.

nodes.name: TestWeakeningReport
nodes.summary: Frozen report of reasons, checked and not-checked paths; completion_state is blocked-escalated or qualified-draft and to_envelope builds a G6_E_* warning-card envelope.

nodes.name: detect_test_weakening
nodes.summary: Compares test, conftest and configuration files before and after a change and returns a TestWeakeningReport listing each sign of weakening and what was not seen.

nodes.name: read_snapshot
nodes.summary: Reads a directory into the path-to-text mapping detect_test_weakening compares, skipping VCS, cache and virtualenv folders and raising on unreadable files.

nodes.name: _kind
nodes.summary: Classifies a path as test, startup, config, runner, data or other for the comparison.

nodes.name: _files
nodes.summary: Normalises one side of the comparison (mapping or directory) into a path-to-text mapping, rejecting other input.

nodes.name: _pytest_settings
nodes.summary: Extracts the pytest settings section from pytest.ini, setup.cfg or pyproject.toml text.

nodes.name: _config_reasons
nodes.summary: Reports changes to pytest settings between the before and after versions of a configuration file.

nodes.name: _python_reasons
nodes.summary: Reports weakening signals in a Python test or startup file: deletion, removed tests or checks, new skips, mocks, patches and hooks.

nodes.name: _facts
nodes.summary: Walks a parsed module to collect the facts compared across versions: tests, checks, markers, hooks and module-level patches.

nodes.name: _checks
nodes.summary: Collects the assertions and assert-style calls in a function, noting ones placed where they cannot fail.

nodes.name: _markers
nodes.summary: Collects skip, xfail and similar markers attached to a test or module.

nodes.name: _is_patch
nodes.summary: Recognises a module-level mock or patch call that runs when pytest imports the file.

nodes.name: _test_reasons
nodes.summary: Compares the per-test facts of old and new versions and reports removed tests, removed checks and early returns.

nodes.name: _imported
nodes.summary: Finds the module names existing tests import so a new file shadowing one can be flagged.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package entry for g6.self_maintenance, theory-of-constraints planning over G6 own work; re-exports the block, its input model and refusal, and declares component metadata, requirements and failure modes.

nodes.name: block.py
nodes.summary: SelfMaintenanceBlock, the registry and MCP door to self-maintenance planning: identify_constraint and a simulated ticket plan over caller-declared stage measurements, returning reliability envelopes and never running anything.

nodes.name: MaintenanceInput
nodes.summary: Pydantic input model for the block: op (help, ops, identify_constraint, plan), day, stages, tickets, ticket_stages, provider and request/run ids, with extra fields forbidden.

nodes.name: SelfMaintenanceBlock
nodes.summary: AIBlock whose infer dispatches the help, ops, identify_constraint and plan operations, mapping results to qualified-draft or blocked-escalated envelopes with G6_E_SELF_MAINTENANCE_* codes.

nodes.name: codes.py
nodes.summary: Stable G6_E_SELF_MAINTENANCE_* error codes (input, constraint, plan, live agent off) and the SelfMaintenanceRefused exception carrying a code and reason.

nodes.name: SelfMaintenanceRefused
nodes.summary: Exception for something the maintenance loop will not do, carrying its stable code and reason.

nodes.name: constraints.py
nodes.summary: Theory-of-constraints scheduler: measured stages, constraint identification from independently observed stages, a safety envelope and non-regression conditions for proposed improvements, and a focus plan ranking tickets for the bottleneck.

nodes.name: StageMeasurement
nodes.summary: Validated measurement of one serial workflow stage (attempts, successes, capacity per day, independent observation) with its effective capacity.

nodes.name: ConstraintAssessment
nodes.summary: Frozen result naming the bottleneck stage, throughput bound, evidence basis, ranked observations and the five focusing steps.

nodes.name: SafetyEnvelope
nodes.summary: Validated hard bounds a candidate must meet: minimum task success and maximum unsafe, unauthorized, false-assurance, fairness-gap and cost-per-success rates.

nodes.name: OutcomeObservation
nodes.summary: Validated observed outcome rates, cost, throughput, independence flag and sample count for a baseline or candidate.

nodes.name: ImprovementDecision
nodes.summary: Frozen decision on a proposed improvement: reliability state, reason, utility delta and a review_only permission.

nodes.name: identify_constraint
nodes.summary: Names the stage with least effective capacity when every stage was independently observed, otherwise returns an unknown bottleneck with a measurement step.

nodes.name: assess_improvement
nodes.summary: Applies necessary conditions to recommend a trial: independent evaluation, enough samples, the safety envelope and no observed regression; never grants deployment.

nodes.name: focus_plan
nodes.summary: Ranks only the tickets tied to the identified bottleneck within the token budget, refusing when the bottleneck is unmeasured or has no ticket.

nodes.name: controller.py
nodes.summary: G6-on-G6 maintenance controller that runs one person-approved, budget-reserved repair cycle on a disposable workspace copy, binding each approval to a ticket, provider and day; the live agent path refuses in this release.

nodes.name: digest.py
nodes.summary: Renders, writes and reads the self-improvement loop's daily Markdown digest, a bounded page of under 60 lines summarising cycles, constraints, failures and findings for a daily human review.

nodes.name: envelope.py
nodes.summary: The loop's durable records and halting machinery: a hash-chained constraint log (CycleLog), STOP file and stop journal handling, canonical stops, admission under an OS-level stop lock, refusal logs, runner lock and heartbeat, all failing closed to G6_E_LOOP_STOP_UNREADABLE.
nodes.languageNotes: Leans on OS-level file locks, fsync-before-act appends and byte-digest bindings so that a stop cannot be lost between processes or across crashes.

nodes.name: experience.py
nodes.summary: Consent-bound product learning: validates aggregate user signals and summarises task completion, time-to-value and satisfaction as a qualified-draft experience summary, plus the obligations for collecting such feedback.

nodes.name: kernel.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic self-maintenance decision kernel: the allowlist of source paths a maintenance change may touch, budget policies, maintenance tickets, an append-only token BudgetBook with reservations, and ticket ranking.

nodes.name: pacing.py
nodes.summary: Weekly per-provider budget pacing for the continuous loop: provider windows from settings.json, target and ceiling curves, account readings, and a BudgetMeter that reserves and settles work against the operator store.

nodes.name: usage.py
nodes.summary: Reads what each provider's own tool reports about account limits (Codex app-server rate limits) and watches Claude and Codex host callers so provider refusals, limits and capacity stops reach the loop as G6 codes, with request identities and an AccountReader for the budget meter.
nodes.languageNotes: Classifies provider stops only from structured JSON/JSONL output, never from model-writable text, and keys request identity on file identity (volume/file id or device/inode) rather than path names.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for governed self-modification: re-exports the patch promotion gate, change-scope and regression-delta inputs, the improvement cycle, rubrics, scorecard store and diagnosis, with a docstring stating capability limits and what was not ported.

nodes.name: cases.py
nodes.summary: Small benchmark case runner that calls trusted application code on asserted cases and produces a RunSummary feeding regression_delta; missing assertions make the run unevaluable.

nodes.name: change_scope.py
nodes.summary: Pure path-scope classifier for a proposed self-modification: blocks deletions, out-of-repo paths, pytest configuration files and paths outside the target component, and routes protected fragments to a person.

nodes.name: diagnosis.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic first classification of why a component audit fell short, using fixed level/score and error-pattern rules and naming the rule that fired, with no confidence number.

nodes.name: improvement_loop.py
nodes.summary: Runs one governed improvement cycle (sense, propose, evaluate, gate, apply, remeasure, roll back) with injected callables, applying only auto-promotable gate decisions on the exact patch and reporting qualified-draft at best.

nodes.name: patch_promotion_gate.py
nodes.summary: Risk-graded, deterministic, down-only promotion gate for proposed harness patches: levels risk, checks protected paths and promotion criteria, and blocks permission expansion, weakened safety, removed human review or irreversible changes.

nodes.name: persistence.py
nodes.summary: ScorecardStore keeping the maturity scorecard as an append-only audit_log.jsonl and a rewritten scorecard.json, with flag-holding level rules and refused promotions.

nodes.name: regression_delta.py
nodes.summary: Compares a test run after a change with a baseline run and answers passed, failed or unevaluable, treating new failures, lost tests and newly skipped tests as regressions.

nodes.name: rubrics.py
nodes.summary: Evaluates a component's output against structured shape assertions, scores rubrics, classifies maturity levels T0-T5 and holds a RubricRegistry loadable from JSON.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic types for the maturity scorecard: rubric assertions and provenance, component rubrics, assertion and rubric scores, audit results, maturity scores and the scorecard, with level names T0-T6.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the skills G6 ships as package data (using-g6 and the vendored superpowers skills), read by g6.core.skills and copied by `g6 skills install`.

nodes.name: routing.py
nodes.summary: Loads, writes and checks the routing manifest (using-g6/routing.json) that marks every MCP tool and component op as agent-facing with a route in the root skill or exempt with a reason, reporting every problem in the join with the code.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Skill guide for the G6 maintenance planner: applying the theory of constraints to a measured workflow with identify_constraint and plan ops, when to use it, failure modes, blind spots and examples.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Skill guide for G6 self-training: the patch promotion gate, improvement cycle, scorecard and their Python API, what a person must approve, failure modes and blind spots.

nodes.name: abstraction.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the separate abstraction MCP server's tools and their order of work, from loading a dataset to proposing, evaluating, refining and saving abstractions.

nodes.name: context.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the Context Engine's g6_knowledge_* tools over the person's own files: adding, searching, reading and revoking sources, reading replies and the consent and exclusion rules.

nodes.name: lifecycle.md
nodes.summary: Reference mapping each stage of a coding agent's lifecycle to its superpowers skill, its G6 step and principle, with the full Python delivery steps and the MCP mission and review-until-clean loops.

nodes.name: rules.md
nodes.summary: Reference for rule reasoning routes: when to use datalog, prolog or graph_reasoning components, sessions of facts over time, and why Experta is retired.

nodes.name: CycleReport
nodes.summary: Frozen record of one maintenance cycle's outcome: state, ticket, provider, reserved and observed usage, evidence, next action and audit head.

nodes.name: cycle_binding
nodes.summary: Digest binding a person's approval of a cycle to the planned ticket, provider and day.

nodes.name: run_one_cycle
nodes.summary: Runs one approved planning, repair and check cycle on a disposable workspace copy: checks the approval, reserves budget, runs the agent and an independent checker, and settles the outcome.

nodes.name: run_existing_agent
nodes.summary: Refuses in this release before any runtime is built, since live agents need the later mission container.

nodes.name: _run_existing_agent_live
nodes.summary: Unreachable adapter for existing Codex/Claude runtimes, kept for a later phase.

nodes.name: _limits
nodes.summary: Builds the digest page's first line: what limits progress, at which level, its evidence and what only the owner can do.

nodes.name: _generation
nodes.summary: Formats one generation entry of the loop for the digest page.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Renders one day's bounded digest page from that day's cycles, the latest named constraint and the loop's current limit.

nodes.name: digest_path
nodes.summary: Path of a day's digest page under the digests folder.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one day's digest page whole or not at all, replacing an earlier write of the same day.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads a day's page, disclosing only one that matches the writer's completed snapshot.

nodes.name: latest
nodes.summary: Returns the newest day's digest page, or None before the first.

nodes.name: _Held
nodes.summary: Stop lock a stop keeps while its canonical record does not stand, released when the request finishes, is unreferenced or its process ends.

nodes.name: CycleLog
nodes.summary: Hash-chained constraint log of the loop: cycles, findings, enrolments, pauses, resumes, starts, stops, provider limits and the failed and quiet streaks that pause the loop.

nodes.name: StopUnreadable
nodes.summary: OSError raised when a file that says whether a stop was asked for cannot be read; readers treat it as a stop in force.

nodes.name: Stop
nodes.summary: One reading of everything a stop decision stands on, with its code (STOPPED, STOP_UNREADABLE or none) and reason.

nodes.name: StopSeen
nodes.summary: One reading of the STOP file, its mtime and the stop journal, with helpers deciding what a start lifts and whether it binds by file, journal, canonical stops or enrolment.

nodes.name: StopReceipt
nodes.summary: String subclass carrying why a folder is stopped plus the stop's canonical identity, legacy entries and whether its record stands.

nodes.name: _begin_stop
nodes.summary: Installs a process-level denial for a stop request before any path work, clock or I/O.

nodes.name: _rules
nodes.summary: Internal rule helper used when validating stop and record fields.

nodes.name: utf8
nodes.summary: Encodes text as UTF-8 by one rule that cannot fail, escaping lone surrogates, so caller text never blocks a stop write.

nodes.name: writable
nodes.summary: Returns a value with every string, keys included, made safe for UTF-8 JSON rows or heartbeats.

nodes.name: utf8_text
nodes.summary: Escapes only code points strict UTF-8 cannot hold, chunked, without truncation.

nodes.name: utf8_fields
nodes.summary: Applies the UTF-8 text policy to names, reasons, notes and nested ledger or reply fields.

nodes.name: fresh_line
nodes.summary: The single rule for where a row ends in every row file, so each append starts on a fresh line.

nodes.name: _absent
nodes.summary: Decides whether a file the open could not find is truly absent, using lstat on entries and refusing links or unlistable folders.

nodes.name: _read_file
nodes.summary: Reads a file's bytes with its prior mtime and OS file identity, or None when it is truly absent.

nodes.name: _parsed
nodes.summary: Parses and checks the constraint log from the bytes a reading took, via the ledger, without reopening the records.

nodes.name: _start_of
nodes.summary: Finds the last start in the log and why a later stop revoked it.

nodes.name: _canonical_stops_on_disk
nodes.summary: Reads the canonical stop records from disk, refusing on any missing, partial or malformed record.

nodes.name: canonical_stops
nodes.summary: Lists pending or failed canonical stop requests, each denying its folder including alternate spellings.

nodes.name: canonical_stop_reason
nodes.summary: Why the canonical stops alone refuse what runs on a start, or an empty string.

nodes.name: canonical_stop_record
nodes.summary: Reads one request's own canonical stop record as a receipt observation.

nodes.name: enrolment_digest
nodes.summary: Digest of the enrolment on record, or the digest of none.

nodes.name: enrolment_id
nodes.summary: Stored identity of the current enrolment write.

nodes.name: stop_in_force
nodes.summary: The single reading that decides whether a stop is in force on a loop folder and why, opening the STOP file, stop journal and records once each under one digest.

nodes.name: stop_seen
nodes.summary: Returns the STOP file and journal as stop_in_force read them, raising StopUnreadable when unreadable.

nodes.name: stop_reason
nodes.summary: Why the STOP file alone halts the loop for the start on record, from stop_in_force's reading.
