nodes.name: _round_robin
nodes.summary: Takes ids round-robin over repository pools until a size is reached, skipping exhausted repositories.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Draws the development, evaluation and scored order splits by the seeded per-class repository rule.

nodes.name: check_disjoint
nodes.summary: Asserts the development and evaluation splits share no repository or id.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads the dataset columns, draws the split and writes it to the results folder.

nodes.name: shadow.py
nodes.summary: V7 shadow learning: after a task where G6's check found something, a model writes one lesson from G6's findings and G's visible outcome into a g6.learning theory store as a candidate, archived as its own run; no lesson reaches Claude Code.

nodes.name: user_text
nodes.summary: Builds the lesson prompt from what G6 found, what became of it and the lessons so far, never the public task id.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses the model reply into a lesson, or a none-with-reason record, raising ValueError when the reply is neither.

nodes.name: after_task
nodes.summary: Writes one shadow lesson after a task: model call through g6.core.llm, candidate theory or recurrence in the store, and a full archived run with cost.

nodes.name: Recorder
nodes.summary: Anthropic SDK client wrapper whose messages.create keeps every response exactly as the API sent it.

nodes.name: v7common.py
nodes.summary: Shared V7 module: frozen settings, spend rules and cap, the provider key redactor, and the write-once archive of run folders indexed by run.json with an append-only runs.jsonl ledger.

nodes.name: cap_usd
nodes.summary: Reads G6_BENCH_MAX_USD (default and ceiling 180); a non-positive value gives 0 so nothing runs.

nodes.name: spend
nodes.summary: Totals spend per phase and runs in flight from the archive ledger records.

nodes.name: may_start
nodes.summary: Decides whether work reserved at a given amount may start under the cap, counting runs in flight.

nodes.name: write_json
nodes.summary: Writes a redacted JSON summary atomically via a temporary file and rename.

nodes.name: Redactor
nodes.summary: Replaces the provider key value and any sk-ant- token in text bound for a file or terminal, and reports leaks.

nodes.name: Archive
nodes.summary: Write-once archive root: append-only runs.jsonl ledger, run folder creation, and lookups of runs and records.

nodes.name: RunFolder
nodes.summary: One write-once run folder: creates files once, streams output, scans for leaked keys and writes the run.json index on finish.

nodes.name: PROTOCOL.md
nodes.summary: Draft V8 protocol: a two-arm feasibility study of whether a failure-theory harness built with G6 recovers more initial failures than Claude Code's self-check under matched caps, on a new Python-only SWE-bench Pro split, with separate engineering evaluation.

nodes.name: sample.py
nodes.summary: Draws V8's Python-only split from pinned SWE-bench Pro metadata with seed 20261027, reusing the two OpenLibrary pilot tasks and excluding V7 development tasks; never loads task text or patches.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Draws the development and scored task ids from Python rows, reusing two OpenLibrary pilots and excluding V7 dev ids.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads pinned metadata and the V7 split, draws the V8 split and writes it.

nodes.name: agentic.py
nodes.summary: Small worked-example helper where a model picks from a fixed menu with a reason via G6's SolverPlanner pattern, falling back to fixed logic when there is no model or the reply is off the menu.

nodes.name: choice
nodes.summary: Returns one option from the menu and a Decision recording whether the model or the fallback chose it.

nodes.name: attrs-1509.md
nodes.summary: Scoring amendment for worked example attrs-1509: explains each test change that removed assertions pinned to the fix's own alias_is_default name while keeping the behaviour checked, with controls and an independent audit.

nodes.name: attrs-1509.patch
nodes.summary: Unified diff amending the attrs-1509 requirement tests (test_functional, test_hooks, test_make, utils) so they no longer pin the fix's private alias_is_default field while still checking aliases and behaviour.

nodes.name: black-5144.md
nodes.summary: Scoring amendment record for task black-5144 (psf/black#4296): explains why the maintainers' exact expected formatting for comments in comprehensions is loosened to no-crash, AST-equivalence, stability and comment-count checks.

nodes.name: black-5144.patch
nodes.summary: Test diff for black-5144 that adds a branch in tests/test_format.py so the comments_in_comprehensions case is scored by assert_format, comment survival and an unchanged for-block instead of a pinned output.
nodes.languageNotes: Unified git diff applied to an upstream project's tests at scoring time; not G6 source.

nodes.name: click-3678.md
nodes.summary: Scoring amendment record for task click-3678 (pallets/click#2819): removes checks pinned to the fix's invented _click_default_help name and warnings, and records the controls showing an alternative documented fix still passes.

nodes.name: click-3678.patch
nodes.summary: Test diff for click-3678 across tests/test_basic.py, tests/test_info_dict.py and tests/test_options.py that drops the reserved-name test, relaxes the stored help-option name to mock.ANY and removes an unstated warning requirement.
nodes.languageNotes: Unified git diff applied to an upstream project's tests at scoring time; not G6 source.

nodes.name: pydantic-13133.md
nodes.summary: Scoring amendment record for task pydantic-13133 (pydantic#10565): replaces a version-branched exact error string with a pattern requiring the project's wording and the failing annotation, including an independent audit's accepted finding.

nodes.name: pydantic-13133.patch
nodes.summary: Test diff for pydantic-13133 rewriting test_invalid_forward_ref in tests/test_forward_ref.py to match the error by pattern rather than an exact, version-specific message.
nodes.languageNotes: Unified git diff applied to an upstream project's tests at scoring time; not G6 source.

nodes.name: starlette-3166.md
nodes.summary: Scoring amendment record for task starlette-3166 (starlette#2019): rewrites session tests to check Set-Cookie behaviour through the public API instead of the fix's Session class, and drops an unstated Vary: Cookie requirement.

nodes.name: starlette-3166.patch
nodes.summary: Test diff for starlette-3166 in tests/middleware/test_session.py that removes the Session import, rewrites test_session_tracks_modification over a real app and response headers, and trims Vary assertions.
nodes.languageNotes: Unified git diff applied to an upstream project's tests at scoring time; not G6 source.

nodes.name: compare.py
nodes.summary: Frozen comparison of the self-correction loop arm against plain Claude Code on held-out bugs: reads saved run verdicts only and reports pass-rate uplift, sign-test p-values, per-bug tallies, a bootstrap interval and a trust table on both maintainers' and amended tests.

nodes.name: convert_cases.json
nodes.summary: Fixed list of conversion-run cases (task, repeat, arm, start right/wrong) that arms X1 and X2 start from, chosen by rule before any run.

nodes.name: distill.py
nodes.summary: Round 3 harness distillation: turns failed training runs into DevFailure records, asks G6's FailureTraceStrategy for new generic agent instructions through a cost-metered model, and refuses text that names a project, test, file or issue.

nodes.name: evolve.py
nodes.summary: Stage 3 harness training: G6's cegis outer loop proposes add-only harness changes per heuristic operator from failure records, screens and runs them, and compares each candidate with its parent bug by bug via the heuristics assess contract.

nodes.name: final_review.py
nodes.summary: Final review step: another model family reads each finished saved patch in a network-less container from the agent image, and its written test runs on parent and patch to classify the review as reproduced, opinion or clean.

nodes.name: G1.txt
nodes.summary: Arm G1's hand-written counterexample-loop instructions for the coding agent: state the rule, enumerate at least six input shapes, check each before and after every repair, and stop only when every shape passes after the last repair.

nodes.name: heuristics.py
nodes.summary: Copy of PR #4's bounded heuristic contracts: Heuristic and Trial dataclasses, a mutate operator that spawns one child per other operator, and assess, which vetoes any candidate that loses a case its baseline solved.

nodes.name: library.py
nodes.summary: Reference-material helper for the proposer: chunks Markdown folders into passages, ranks passages by shared long words, and refuses proposer text that copies an eight-word run from any passage.

nodes.name: loop_model.py
nodes.summary: Encodes the self-correction loop's stop rule as a small symbolic state model and uses G6's model checker to test the honest_stop invariant for the old rule, the new rule and the new rule without reruns.
nodes.languageNotes: Transition relations are written as SMT-LIB strings composed by small Python helpers, then checked by bounded model checking and k-induction.

nodes.name: loop.py
nodes.summary: Round 3 distillation loop driver: runs a baseline, then cegis generations whose search distils new harness text from failures and whose evaluation runs every training bug through run.py, then one held-out look; also rescores saved runs on amended tests.

nodes.name: observe.py
nodes.summary: Transcript analysis for G6 launch fixes W1-W5: reads an archived Claude Code stream to report whether the g6 server started, reply sizes and refusals, whether reports were shown verbatim, template-instance handling, and G6's own proposer outcomes.

nodes.name: PLAN.md
nodes.summary: The pre-registered plan for worked examples on well-known Python projects: projects, tasks, validation, run flow, independent check, spend and reporting, followed by a dated log of every later change (rounds 2-3, arms A-X, amendments, loop stages and freezes).

nodes.name: probe_replay.py
nodes.summary: Replays every archived scout's probe set against every archived patch of a training bug and the maintainers' fix, without any model call, to measure which probe sets are wrong and which have power.

nodes.name: RESULTS.md
nodes.summary: Running results of the worked examples: how runs were made, each run in order, a defect found in G6, corrections, runs 6-10, round 2 with G6's own model, and round 3 formal-methods arms A, E and G1.

nodes.name: round2_g6.py
nodes.summary: Round 2 image-side patcher that edits a copy of G6's verification_search.py and patch_review.py so every review turns on G6's check proposer, failing unless each anchor is found exactly once.

nodes.name: run.py
nodes.summary: The worked examples' main runner: builds base, task and oracle Docker images, validates FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS, runs the key check, drives headless Claude Code with the using-g6 skill across many experiment arms (scouts, critics, CEGIS repair loops, review-until-clean), and performs the independent check into a write-once archive.
nodes.languageNotes: Sibling modules are imported by inserting the script folder into sys.path, so the scanner does not resolve them; all Docker calls use list arguments with no shell.

nodes.name: SELECTION.md
nodes.summary: Selection record for the worked examples: which Python projects were chosen, which pull requests were read (newest first) and turned into tasks, and the run order.

nodes.name: saved
nodes.summary: Collects each saved run's verdicts on maintainers' and amended tests, treating missing verdicts as neither pass nor failure.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Compares one arm with another on the same bugs and repeats, counting wins and losses where both runs exist.

nodes.name: by_bug
nodes.summary: Counts the bugs on which the loop passed more, fewer or the same runs, since repeats of one bug are not independent.

nodes.name: interval
nodes.summary: Computes the 95% uplift interval through G6's compare_methods, resampling whole bugs.

nodes.name: trust
nodes.summary: Tabulates, for each thing an arm said of its own runs, how often that run was actually right.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Builds every arm comparison on both scores, plus control arms reported beside the frozen rule.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that loads task sets and saved rows and prints the frozen comparison reports.

nodes.name: failures
nodes.summary: Builds one DevFailure per failed run from saved rows and archived outputs, truncating patch and output text.

nodes.name: Metered
nodes.summary: Wraps an LLM caller and accumulates an upper-bound cost estimate from characters per call.

nodes.name: distill
nodes.summary: Produces new agent instructions from a base text and failures via FailureTraceStrategy, returning what the text wrongly names.

nodes.name: verdicts
nodes.summary: Lists an arm's saved runs on given tasks, each marked pass or fail on the amended tests.

nodes.name: near_miss
nodes.summary: Summarises what the runner's own checks caught on a run's first patch and what became of it, for the proposer.

nodes.name: diverse
nodes.summary: Selects up to a limit of failure records, cycling bugs and putting failed runs first.

nodes.name: records
nodes.summary: Gathers an arm's failure records (failed runs and near misses), refusing bugs a harness is judged on.

nodes.name: paired
nodes.summary: Compares a candidate harness with its parent bug by bug using heuristics.assess, counting a bug solved if any run passed.

nodes.name: Training
nodes.summary: cegis runner adapter for harness training: search asks G6's proposer for an add-only change to a chosen harness field, evaluate screens it and then runs it on training bugs.

nodes.name: train
nodes.summary: Runs cegis over candidate harness changes from a parent arm and returns the best arm with each candidate's history.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that reads the key, builds the model caller and starts harness training.

nodes.name: review
nodes.summary: Runs one cross-model review of a saved patch in its own network-less container and runs its test on the parent and on the patch.

nodes.name: waiting
nodes.summary: Lists finished runs whose distinct patch has no review yet, in digest order.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that reviews each waiting patch for the training bugs and saves results by patch digest.

nodes.name: Heuristic
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass naming a harness heuristic by id, operator, parent and generation.

nodes.name: Trial
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass receipt of one candidate-versus-baseline case with successes, costs and evaluator digest.

nodes.name: mutate
nodes.summary: Returns child heuristics, one per other operator, bounded by child count and generation depth.

nodes.name: assess
nodes.summary: Evaluates a candidate on fixed cases, validates receipts, and recommends it only with benefit and no regression, labelled qualified-draft.

nodes.name: chunks
nodes.summary: Splits each folder's Markdown into paragraph passages joined up to a character limit.

nodes.name: passages
nodes.summary: Returns the passages sharing the most long words with a query, without any embedding model.

nodes.name: copied
nodes.summary: Checks whether text contains a run of eight words from any source passage, so copied text is refused.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Checks the honest_stop invariant by bounded search and, if not violated, attempts k-induction to report holds_by_induction.

nodes.name: finishes
nodes.summary: Reports whether the model can reach a stop at all, guarding against a vacuous rule.

nodes.name: last_json
nodes.summary: Merges every JSON object printed in a runner's output into one record.

nodes.name: one
nodes.summary: Runs one task and repeat through run.py plus its independent check, saving the result once under loop/.

nodes.name: rescore
nodes.summary: Rescores every saved run of an amended bug on the amended tests and saves the result beside it.

nodes.name: round_of
nodes.summary: Runs one arm across tasks and repeats and returns their rows.

nodes.name: Generations
nodes.summary: cegis runner adapter over harness text: search distils the next generation from failures and evaluate runs it on every training bug.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry for the distillation loop: baseline, generations under the spend stop, then the held-out round.

nodes.name: _report
nodes.summary: Extracts G6's report text from a parsed review reply.

nodes.name: observe
nodes.summary: Scans transcript objects for g6 server startup, review replies, verbatim report display and template-instance refusals.

nodes.name: _assessment
nodes.summary: Finds the first nested dict holding a completion, G6's full assessment.

nodes.name: proposer_summary
nodes.summary: Summarises what G6's own model did in one review: outcome, reasons and proposer activity.

nodes.name: observe_run
nodes.summary: Applies observe to an archived run folder's stream.jsonl, resolving replies Claude Code saved to files.

nodes.name: summary
nodes.summary: Parses one pytest run's counts and failing ids, marking whether any test ran.

nodes.name: replay_task
nodes.summary: Runs every archived probe set on every archived patch and the maintainers' fix for one task inside a container.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Renders the code-by-probe-set result matrix, marking patches the maintainers' tests accept.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that replays probes for each training task and prints the matrices.

nodes.name: patch
nodes.summary: Applies anchor-based text edits, raising ValueError unless each anchor occurs exactly once.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Patches verification_search.py and patch_review.py in a given folder, writing only after every edit's anchor is found.

nodes.name: Task
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one worked-example task (project, PR, issue, merge and parent commits, test modules, install steps) with name and repo path properties.

nodes.name: ProbeRun
nodes.summary: Result of one probe-set run read from pytest's own report, with ran and usable properties so unreadable runs never count as clean.

nodes.name: Repairs
nodes.summary: cegis adapter over the agent's work: search sends the agent what failed, evaluate runs the runner-held probes, and already-seen failures are not resent.

nodes.name: Docker
nodes.summary: Thin docker CLI wrapper through subprocess with list arguments and no shell, offering call, sh and popen.

nodes.name: Context
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding a run's archive, docker handle, key/issue/tree readers, G6 info, critic, round variant, arm, model and repeat; client_env passes the provider key only when one is given.

nodes.name: trained
nodes.summary: Returns what harness training added for a trained L or M arm, as committed before it ran.

nodes.name: scout_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the scout's prompt for an L or M arm, choosing the scout method version by generation.

nodes.name: split_failures
nodes.summary: Classifies failing probe cases into counterexamples (passed at base, fail now) and other failures using G6's plan rule.

nodes.name: failures_of
nodes.summary: Collects failing ids across probe sets and builds the message the agent reads, regressions first and capped.

nodes.name: critic_report
nodes.summary: Parses the critic's reply into rule, verdict, reasons and test, ignoring progress lines.

nodes.name: run_codex
nodes.summary: Runs one read-only Codex task on a pack through the Codex companion script.

nodes.name: scout_gate
nodes.summary: Judges a scout's probes by the runner's own count: pytest exit, collected cases, crashes and G6 InputDomain combination counts.

nodes.name: prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the run's prompt per round and arm, including G6 instructions, harness addenda and issue discussion.

nodes.name: base_dockerfile
nodes.summary: Renders the base image Dockerfile installing G6 as its README does plus a pinned Claude Code.

nodes.name: task_dockerfile
nodes.summary: Renders a task image Dockerfile holding upstream's base commit alone with the project's virtual environment.

nodes.name: oracle_dockerfile
nodes.summary: Renders the oracle image Dockerfile adding the maintainers' fix kept apart in /oracle.

nodes.name: _completions
nodes.summary: Collects every completion.activities list nested under an object, outermost first.

nodes.name: g6_model_cost
nodes.summary: Prices G6's own model calls in full assessments at published prices with no cache discount.

nodes.name: r3_loop_key
nodes.summary: Maps a round 3 loop run to its schedule key across A, E, G and H arms.

nodes.name: r3_refusal
nodes.summary: Enforces round 3's rules: scheduled arm/model/repeat, run order across models, per-run cap and the round's spend stop.

nodes.name: r3_ledger
nodes.summary: Appends one ledger line per round 3 run with its cost and the round's running spend.

nodes.name: hook_script
nodes.summary: Renders the shell script the Stop hook uses to run the probes against the working tree.

nodes.name: stop_hook
nodes.summary: Renders arm L's Stop hook that blocks stopping only on a failing probe and lets go after a maximum number of blocks.

nodes.name: scout_tree
nodes.summary: Reads a scout's tree.json as PR #5's GoalTree, reporting shapes and those without a probe.

nodes.name: parse_junit
nodes.summary: Parses JUnit XML into per-case outcomes keyed classname::name, keeping the worst outcome.

nodes.name: keyprobe_driver
nodes.summary: Returns the driver script that checks, under G6's confined review, that a test cannot see the provider key while an unconfined control can.

nodes.name: _reports
nodes.summary: Collects every nested dict with a report and an outcome, i.e. G6 assessments.

nodes.name: extract_rounds
nodes.summary: Splits a transcript into review rounds: each g6_review_patch input, its metaharness_job polls, and the final outcome.

nodes.name: read_stream
nodes.summary: Feeds Claude Code's stream-json output to a tally until it ends or hits a timeout, turn cap or cost cap.

nodes.name: status_of
nodes.summary: Maps a stream stop reason and tally into the run's final status.

nodes.name: redact_tree
nodes.summary: Masks the provider key in every file under a folder copied out of a container.

nodes.name: key_check
nodes.summary: Runs the key check in a network-less container from the run's image, confirming the confined test cannot read the key.

nodes.name: start_net
nodes.summary: Creates the run's internal docker network and egress proxy container.

nodes.name: refusal
nodes.summary: Returns why a run may not start (HOLD file, commit, validation or stop), or an empty string.

nodes.name: hook_selftest
nodes.summary: Dry-run self-test of the round hook: changes the working tree and runs the hook as Claude Code would.

nodes.name: run_task
nodes.summary: Runs one task end to end, refusing before start when the commit, validation or stop disallows it, and cleaning containers it started.

nodes.name: run_session
nodes.summary: Runs one Claude Code session in the container and saves its stream, returning how it ended.

nodes.name: probe_gate
nodes.summary: Applies scout_gate to probes in a folder using the container's pytest exit, cross-test cases and crash counts.

nodes.name: run_set
nodes.summary: Runs one probe set on the current tree, copying hidden sets in and removing them so the agent cannot read them.

nodes.name: run_critic
nodes.summary: Runs arm L8's cross-model critic on the finished patch on the host, then runs its test on the agent's tree.

nodes.name: run_scout
nodes.summary: Runs arm L's scout session, resets the repository to base, and gates its probes and goal tree before any fix.

nodes.name: repair_loop
nodes.summary: Runs G6's cegis over the agent's finished work, sending probe failures back for repair until clean or capped.

nodes.name: reviews_until_clean
nodes.summary: Arm K: plain Claude Code, then cross-model reviews and same-session repairs until no reviewed defect reproduces.

nodes.name: review_once
nodes.summary: Arm R control: one cross-model review and at most one repair if its test reproduces a defect.

nodes.name: _run_task
nodes.summary: Core run body: builds the container and prompt, runs scout, sessions, hooks, critics and repair loops per arm, then archives the patch, transcript, rounds and costs.

nodes.name: _oracle_run
nodes.summary: Runs code (parent, maintainers' fix or a patch) with chosen tests in a fresh network-less oracle container and parses JUnit results.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Validates a task: computes FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS with no network and no model.

nodes.name: amend
nodes.summary: Runs the amended tests' own controls and refuses a diff that leaves no test distinguishing parent from fix.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: The independent check of a run's final and per-round patches against the validated or amended test lists.

nodes.name: selfcheck
nodes.summary: Control for the independent check: scores the maintainers' fix as if it were the agent's patch.

nodes.name: g6replay
nodes.summary: Replays G6's own confined review on the maintainers' fix or a patch for judging a finding.

nodes.name: modelcheck
nodes.summary: Round 2 pre-run check: one call to G6's model from a task container through the proxy, cost counted at an upper bound.

nodes.name: build_base
nodes.summary: Builds and records G6's base image from a ref's commit with a pinned Claude Code binary.

nodes.name: build_images
nodes.summary: Builds a task's agent image and oracle image for a G6 commit.

nodes.name: read_thread
nodes.summary: Returns the issue comments made before the fix's pull request opened.

nodes.name: brief
nodes.summary: Formats a short terminal view of a record, counting rather than listing test results.

nodes.name: progress
nodes.summary: Reads a running or finished run's stream to report model calls, cost so far, rounds and the last tool used.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry dispatching base, images, validate, selfcheck, freecheck, modelcheck, run, check, amend, replay and progress commands.

nodes.name: selection.py
nodes.summary: Read-only script applying PLAN.md's selection rule for worked-example bug tasks: screens 15 candidate Python projects against licence, star, PyPI-download and benchmark-overlap rules (P1, P2, P4) via the GitHub CLI, then applies the mechanical task checks T1, T3 and T4 to merged pull requests and writes candidates.json to the archive.
nodes.languageNotes: Inserts its own folder on sys.path to import the sibling wecommon module, and is named 'selection' so it never shadows the standard library's select module.

nodes.name: project_rules
nodes.summary: Applies project rules P1 (top-100 PyPI), P2 (10k stars, permissive licence) and P4 (not a SWE-bench or Multimodal repository) to one candidate and returns the verdict with reasons.

nodes.name: is_test
nodes.summary: Classifies a repository path as a test file by directory or test_/_test naming conventions.

nodes.name: t3
nodes.summary: Rule T3: checks that a pull request changes Python source and also touches at least one test file.

nodes.name: t1
nodes.summary: Rule T1: checks that a pull request was merged into the default branch inside the selection window.

nodes.name: t4
nodes.summary: Rule T4: checks that the merge commit's files match the pull request's files and stay within size limits.

nodes.name: gh_runner
nodes.summary: Runs a GitHub CLI command as a subprocess and returns its stdout, raising on failure.

nodes.name: merged_prs
nodes.summary: Lists a project's merged pull requests through gh pr list, newest first, failing if the listing may be truncated.

nodes.name: issue
nodes.summary: Fetches one GitHub issue's title, labels, state and truncated body for a person's T2 judgement.

nodes.name: screen
nodes.summary: Screens one project's merged pull requests through T1, T3 and T4 and attaches the linked issue text for each that passes.

nodes.name: top_pypi
nodes.summary: Downloads the published top-PyPI-packages list used by rule P1.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: resolves the archive, applies project rules to each candidate, screens kept projects and writes candidates.json.

nodes.name: wecommon.py
nodes.summary: Shared helpers for the worked-example scripts: the write-once run archive outside the repository with its runs.jsonl index, Anthropic model prices and cost accounting for Claude Code stream-json output, the provider-key redactor, and the $100 spending stop.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dataclasses with @property accessors for derived costs and a write-once folder discipline that raises ArchiveError rather than overwriting.

nodes.name: now
nodes.summary: Returns the current UTC time as an ISO-8601 timestamp string.

nodes.name: archive_root
nodes.summary: Resolves the worked-examples archive folder from G6_WE_ARCHIVE or a home-relative default.

nodes.name: sha256_file
nodes.summary: Streams a file through SHA-256 and returns its hex digest.

nodes.name: price_of
nodes.summary: Looks up per-token prices for a model name, falling back to the highest published prices for unknown models.

nodes.name: usage_cost
nodes.summary: Computes the dollar cost of one usage record, splitting cache writes into 5-minute and 1-hour rates.

nodes.name: model_usage_cost
nodes.summary: Sums the cost over a result record's per-model usage map.

nodes.name: Redactor
nodes.summary: Masks an provider key's value and any sk-ant- token in text bound for a file or terminal, and reports leaks.

nodes.name: Tally
nodes.summary: Dataclass that consumes Claude Code stream-json lines and tallies distinct model calls, token usage and cost from the stream, the result record and the reported total.

nodes.name: ArchiveError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the archive refuses to overwrite an existing run folder or file.

nodes.name: RunFolder
nodes.summary: Write-once run folder: writes redacted text and JSON files, refuses existing names, and records the run's end and cost in the archive index.

nodes.name: Archive
nodes.summary: The run archive root: appends to and reads runs.jsonl, and starts uniquely timestamped run folders.

nodes.name: spent
nodes.summary: Totals dollars spent from the archive index, charging a started-but-unended run its full stop amount.

nodes.name: may_start
nodes.summary: Decides whether another run may start without the spend plus the run's stop exceeding the cap.

nodes.name: tasks_dev.json
nodes.summary: Stage 3 task list of bugs for G6 to learn from, in repositories kept apart from stage 2; currently empty.

nodes.name: tasks_fresh.json
nodes.summary: Fresh bug tasks for judging the loop on unseen bugs: per task the project, licence, PR and issue numbers, merge and parent commits, test modules and install commands, plus a dropped list.

nodes.name: tasks_unseen.json
nodes.summary: Stage 2 task list of bugs from repositories never used in training, drawn by PLAN.md's rule; currently empty.

nodes.name: tasks.json
nodes.summary: The worked-example tasks chosen by PLAN.md's selection rule in run order, each with repository, PR, issue, merge commit, test modules, install commands and environment.

nodes.name: at_mapping.json
nodes.summary: Maps acceptance tests AT-001 to AT-010 of specification G6-UX-VALUE-001 to the owner's text by SHA-256 digest and to the tests and fixtures that check each, with scope (0.3.0, partial, deferred) and gate.

nodes.name: decisions.json
nodes.summary: Records one entry per workflow-view gate run (manifest digest, row, results, decision); the view's admitted level in code must equal what these entries admit.

nodes.name: G2.json
nodes.summary: Frozen decision manifest for gate G2, measuring the narrow view (outcome, one obstacle, one next check, G6's cost) against the existing report alone: cases, labels, unit, eligible starts, baseline and comparison, agent/information/budget policies, preservation checks, clocks, handling of failed starts, disclosures, costs and per-row thresholds.

nodes.name: G3.json
nodes.summary: Frozen decision manifest for gate G3, measuring diagnosis hypotheses against the narrow view, with blind labels from the owner and one Codex reviewer: cases, labels, unit, eligible starts, baseline and comparison, agent/information/budget policies, preservation checks, clocks, handling of failed starts, disclosures, costs and per-row thresholds.

nodes.name: G4.json
nodes.summary: Frozen decision manifest for gate G4, measuring at most three suggestions with person-made decisions against the diagnosis view: cases, labels, unit, eligible starts, baseline and comparison, agent/information/budget policies, preservation checks, clocks, handling of failed starts, disclosures, costs and per-row thresholds.

nodes.name: G5.json
nodes.summary: Frozen decision manifest for gate G5, measuring the optional feedback question and value row with invited outside developers: cases, labels, unit, eligible starts, baseline and comparison, agent/information/budget policies, preservation checks, clocks, handling of failed starts, disclosures, costs and per-row thresholds.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Protocol for measuring the section 17 workflow view: the G2 to G5 gate order, what each file in the folder holds, the rules every run follows, the evidence owed per gate, and how to run the contracts.

nodes.name: run_contracts.py
nodes.summary: Runs section 17's local deterministic workflow contracts: feeds each JSON fixture under tests/workflow/fixtures/contracts through the named workflow function (obstacles, friction, view, lifecycle, diagnose, decisions, feedback and more) in a scratch G6_HOME and compares against frozen expected output, counting unsupported definite claims and unauthorised disclosures; also simulates sessions to measure what the view adds.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports g6 modules lazily inside each runner and dispatches fixtures through a RUNNERS name-to-function table; a contextmanager isolates and restores G6_HOME and workflow environment variables.

nodes.name: sha
nodes.summary: Returns the SHA-256 hex digest of a UTF-8 string, used to derive deterministic project, task and run ids.

nodes.name: _event
nodes.summary: Converts a fixture event row into a workflow record Event with derived run id, digests, refs and timestamps.

nodes.name: _home
nodes.summary: Context manager providing a scratch G6_HOME with the workflow record on, restoring the caller's environment afterwards.

nodes.name: _grant
nodes.summary: Grants cloud-sharing consent for a source through the real consent dialog path using an always-accepting fake session.

nodes.name: _store
nodes.summary: Writes fixture events into the scratch project record, starting runs and mapping fixture run aliases to real run ids.

nodes.name: _identities
nodes.summary: Contract runner checking run and event identity across record restarts, starts and appends.

nodes.name: _view
nodes.summary: Contract runner that stores events, optionally grants consent and builds the workflow view block at a given level.

nodes.name: _lifecycle
nodes.summary: Contract runner exercising record export, corrections, deletion and expiry, returning steps, files, receipts and anything written outside the record.

nodes.name: _diagnose
nodes.summary: Contract runner calling the workflow diagnose step and reporting status, hypothesis rule codes, obstacles and lines.

nodes.name: _decisions
nodes.summary: Contract runner replaying dismiss, reopen and adopt decisions across shows and reporting which suggestions are offered and why any return.

nodes.name: _feedback
nodes.summary: Contract runner for the optional feedback question's rules over a clock: may-invite checks, invitations, closing and opt-in or opt-out.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs every fixture through its named runner, collecting matched counts, mismatches, unsupported definite claims and unauthorised disclosures.

nodes.name: simulate
nodes.summary: Puts synthetic sessions through the workflow view to measure added block lines, build time and reserved questions for a gate's mechanical bars.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: runs the contracts on a folder, prints the result JSON and exits 1 on any mismatch, definite claim or disclosure.

nodes.name: .gitattributes
nodes.summary: Git attributes for the web tree marking vendored static files as binary-safe (-text) so line-ending conversion never changes the bytes pinned by SHA-256.

nodes.name: bundles.md
nodes.summary: Site page introducing worked examples: ready-made bundles of G6 components a person can open and use.

nodes.name: contribute.md
nodes.summary: Short site page on how to contribute to G6 and how to report a security problem.

nodes.name: developers.md
nodes.summary: Developer quickstart for the site: running a task through the harness, using components directly, MCP use from a coding agent, model choice, stopping G6, tuning, the Context Engine, cloud-sharing consent and the workflow record.

nodes.name: faq.md
nodes.summary: Site FAQ covering why G6 exists, the basics, the result labels verified, qualified-draft and blocked-escalated, components and worked examples, safety, the meta-harness and the project.

nodes.name: guide.md
nodes.summary: Long-form guide 'Failure and Harness Engineering for AI Agents': why AI code fails, the four harness layers, failure-diagnosis patterns, self-training without fine-tuning, getting started with G6, and an SDLC prompt library appendix.

nodes.name: install.md
nodes.summary: No-programming getting-started page: choose and open a worked example, pick an AI model if needed, use it, and how data is handled.

nodes.name: metaharness.md
nodes.summary: Site page on tuning G6 to a person's own work with the meta-harness: what it did on one computer, the loop, recovery when it finds nothing, what it may change, and Python and MCP usage.

nodes.name: archive_benchmarks.json
nodes.summary: Site data table of G6's earlier per-component benchmark studies (April to June 2026) with audited figures, baselines, audit status, library coverage and re-run candidacy.

nodes.name: component_catalogue.json
nodes.summary: Generated site catalogue of G6 components: per component its family, package, summary, failure mode, needs, vetting kinds and hidden reason, with counts and a dropped list, transformed from the extension tracker.

nodes.name: from_tracker.py
nodes.summary: One-off, idempotent transform kept as the record of how component_catalogue.json was made: merges extension-tracker CSV rows into the catalogue, removing DROP rows, hiding HOLD and untracked rows, and assigning family, package and vetting kinds.

nodes.name: read_tracker
nodes.summary: Reads every extension-tracker CSV into a component-keyed map, refusing duplicate components.

nodes.name: transform
nodes.summary: Builds the new catalogue from tracker and old catalogue: drops, hides, assigns family, package and vetting, asserts family rules, and computes counts.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that runs the transform and rewrites component_catalogue.json, printing the counts.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Describes the two site data files: component_catalogue.json (the extension rows the Components page lists, made once from the extension tracker, with family, package and vetting kinds) and archive_benchmarks.json (earlier audited benchmark studies shown on the Research page, with an audit_status table).

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the g6site Django project package that holds settings and the root URL configuration.

nodes.name: settings.py
nodes.summary: Django settings for the static g6solver.com site: no database, sessions or accounts, a fixed non-secret key, the pages app, template context processors from pages.context and pages.kinetic, and the static files directory.

nodes.name: urls.py
nodes.summary: Root URL configuration that mounts the three page namespaces (pages, docs_hub, blog) at the site root by including their URL modules.

nodes.name: manage.py
nodes.summary: Django management entry point for the website, used to preview it with runserver or export it with build_static.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the pages Django app that renders every public page of the site.

nodes.name: apps.py
nodes.summary: Django AppConfig declaring the pages application.

nodes.name: blog_urls.py
nodes.summary: URL patterns for the blog (Essays) namespace, generated from the shared page table with one view per page.

nodes.name: catalogue.py
nodes.summary: Reads G6's core components and family extensions from the component registry so the home lattice, component table and Components page cannot drift from the code; holds the plain-language titles (PLAIN), the periodic TABLE and the formal-methods grouping.
nodes.languageNotes: lru_cache on registry reads plus fresh-copy accessors keep cached rows immutable to callers.

nodes.name: clients.py
nodes.summary: Per-client instructions for connecting agents and MCP clients to the g6-mcp stdio server, plus model provider snippets, rendered on the Get started page.

nodes.name: context.py
nodes.summary: Template context processor exposing the site URL, the G6 version read from the library source without importing it, and the current year.

nodes.name: docs_urls.py
nodes.summary: URL patterns for the docs_hub namespace, generated from the shared page table with one view per page.

nodes.name: evidence.py
nodes.summary: Builds the Research page's evidence from committed study results, validation rounds and the audited archive of earlier benchmarks: studies, rounds, paired sign tests, a ledger of with/without-G6 outcomes and a single-change component sweep; a missing file raises rather than showing a partial wall.

nodes.name: extensions.py
nodes.summary: Lists G6 extensions for the site: rows from data/component_catalogue.json joined with the component registry and certificate state (g6.core.vetting), deciding in-library, awaiting-certificate, merged and planned status, all behind the single SHOW_PLANNED switch.

nodes.name: failure_map.py
nodes.summary: Builds the failure-mode map from catalog/failure_modes.json, grouping modes into guarded, planned and unguarded and linking each guard or cause to its Components page entry.

nodes.name: guard.py
nodes.summary: Checks on rendered pages: finds online-service (SaaS) wording with inflection and look-alike character handling and an allow-list, extracts internal and relative links, and collects inline scripts for CSP hashing.
nodes.languageNotes: Regex patterns are generated per guard term, accepting inflections and hyphen/space variants so wording cannot be respelled around the check.

nodes.name: kinetic.py
nodes.summary: Context processor deciding which pages get scroll-driven heading animation (KINETIC) and Bauhaus background forms (BAUHAUS).

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the pages app's Django management package.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the pages app's custom management commands.

nodes.name: build_static.py
nodes.summary: The build_static management command: renders every page in the page table, refuses to write if any page fails, links to a missing path or reads like an online service, then writes HTML, static files, 404, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, _redirects and a CSP _headers file for Cloudflare Pages.

nodes.name: narrative.py
nodes.summary: The home page's story of model limits (hallucination, memory, learning, reasoning, cost and more), each with its cause, G6's answer, the core components that answer it and the essay that goes deeper.

nodes.name: routes.py
nodes.summary: The single table of public pages (Page records for templates, Markdown, placeholders and per-mode failure pages, plus the 21 essays) and the old-URL redirects, read by URL routes, the sitemap and the static export so they cannot disagree.

nodes.name: theory.py
nodes.summary: Data describing the theory documents in docs/theory/ for the Research page: full titles, what each is, key points and the basis it rests on.

nodes.name: urls.py
nodes.summary: URL patterns for the main pages namespace, generated from the shared page table with one view per page.
nodes.languageNotes: URL patterns are built by a list comprehension over a shared PAGES table, with one closure view per page from view_for.

nodes.name: views.py
nodes.summary: One view per page kind (template, Markdown, placeholder, failure mode): builds render-time contexts for the home, components, get-started, graph, research and failure-mode pages, and renders content Markdown with site links, mermaid figures and planned-text filtering.

nodes.name: PagesConfig
nodes.summary: Django AppConfig naming the pages app.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Returns the periodic TABLE columns with each component's short plain title and description.

nodes.name: _rows
nodes.summary: Cached read of every registered core (non-family) component: maturity, docstring summary, plain words, required components and MCP exposure.

nodes.name: components
nodes.summary: Returns fresh copies of every registered core component row, sorted by name.

nodes.name: core_groups
nodes.summary: Splits the core harness into the formal-methods engines and the remaining checks, gates and tuning components.

nodes.name: _extension_rows
nodes.summary: Cached read of every registered family package with its family, maturity, sensitive operations and awaiting-certificate state.

nodes.name: family_members
nodes.summary: Returns copies of every registered package that declares a family.

nodes.name: library_extensions
nodes.summary: Family members not waiting for their certificate, i.e. the extensions in the library.

nodes.name: awaiting_review
nodes.summary: Family members built in a vetted area whose certificate is not current.

nodes.name: lattice
nodes.summary: The home page lattice: all core components with the meta-harness at its centre.

nodes.name: Client
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing how one agent or MCP client registers the g6-mcp server: CLI command, config file, language, snippet and docs link.

nodes.name: Model
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing a model provider option with its configuration snippet and docs link.

nodes.name: g6_version
nodes.summary: Reads __version__ from src/g6/__init__.py with a regex, cached, so the site need not import the library.

nodes.name: site
nodes.summary: Context processor returning SITE_URL, G6_VERSION and the current year to every template.

nodes.name: studies
nodes.summary: Builds the Study list from the study REGISTRY and committed results (V1, V2, adaptation and pilot), raising if a registered study is missing.

nodes.name: rounds
nodes.summary: Reads each validation round's scoreboard and splits into a Study with per-workflow adaptation groups.

nodes.name: both_modes
nodes.summary: Summarises the latest round's rows in both modes, pairing arms per task and counting tuned workflows.

nodes.name: headline
nodes.summary: Returns the headline result groups for the home and Research pages from the adaptation results.

nodes.name: latest_round_speed
nodes.summary: Collects how tuning changed speed in the latest validation round per workflow.

nodes.name: learned_change
nodes.summary: Describes the change the latest round's tuning learned, read from its tuning files.

nodes.name: paired
nodes.summary: Counts cases one arm solved and the other did not (and the reverse) and returns the exact one-sided sign test p-value.

nodes.name: winners
nodes.summary: Per task set of the V6b headline study: G6's best option, what it changed, and a paired comparison against the model alone, labelled post-hoc and unadjusted.

nodes.name: headline_facts
nodes.summary: Computes the headline counts (tasks, workflows, wins, p-values) quoted in page copy.

nodes.name: _registered_entries
nodes.summary: Ledger entries for registered studies (V1, V2, adaptation) computed from their result files.

nodes.name: _pilot_entry
nodes.summary: Ledger entry for the V6 pilot computed from its post-run rows.

nodes.name: _archive_entry
nodes.summary: Converts an archived benchmark row into a ledger Entry with parsed percentages, outcome and scope.

nodes.name: ledger
nodes.summary: Every with/without-G6 comparison: rounds, registered studies, the pilot and audited archive rows, in a fixed order.

nodes.name: ledger_by_scope
nodes.summary: Groups ledger entries by their library scope.

nodes.name: _change_label
nodes.summary: Turns a single tuning change field and value into a short readable label.

nodes.name: component_sweep
nodes.summary: Reads round-01's single-change sweep and tabulates each change's effect per workflow.

nodes.name: sweep_extremes
nodes.summary: Returns the best and worst single changes from the component sweep.

nodes.name: archive
nodes.summary: Loads archive_benchmarks.json and checks each audit_status is a known value.

nodes.name: context
nodes.summary: Assembles the Research page context: theory documents, rounds, headline, winners, both-mode results, the ledger by scope, the component sweep and study counts.

nodes.name: Bar
nodes.summary: Frozen record for one bar in a result chart: arm, label, value, sample size and highlight flag.

nodes.name: Group
nodes.summary: A labelled group of bars with helpers for row scaling, lookup by arm and the best G6 option.

nodes.name: Study
nodes.summary: A registered study or validation round as the Research page shows it, with status, verdict, groups and a tone for its badge.

nodes.name: Entry
nodes.summary: One ledger line comparing results without and with G6 for a study, round or archived benchmark, with outcome, scope and source.

nodes.name: _from_package
nodes.summary: Describes a library package from itself: docstring summary, mitigated failure-mode titles, outside needs and MCP exposure.

nodes.name: _merged
nodes.summary: Decides whether a row joining another package is already merged into the library, respecting certificate state.

nodes.name: vetting_required
nodes.summary: Returns the vetted areas a catalogue row must wait on.

nodes.name: _status
nodes.summary: Computes a catalogue row's displayed status (in library, awaiting certificate, vetted) from the registry and vetting.

nodes.name: rows
nodes.summary: Every catalogue row the page lists, filtering planned rows unless SHOW_PLANNED or planned=True.

nodes.name: extensions
nodes.summary: Extensions of their own, ordered by family then name, each with merged-in and joined rows.

nodes.name: families
nodes.summary: Groups extensions by family with the family package's shared rows.

nodes.name: into_core
nodes.summary: Rows merged into or planned for core harness packages, grouped by package.

nodes.name: named
nodes.summary: Returns named catalogue rows in order, raising LookupError for any name not listed so examples cannot drift.

nodes.name: capabilities
nodes.summary: Capability groups with their listed rows and counts of how many named extensions are in the library.

nodes.name: counts
nodes.summary: Counts of listed extensions, in-library, awaiting, joining, merged and into-core rows.

nodes.name: modes
nodes.summary: Cached load of catalog/failure_modes.json as a tuple of mode records.

nodes.name: context
nodes.summary: Failure-modes page context: modes grouped into guarded, planned and unguarded with counts, depending on SHOW_PLANNED.

nodes.name: mode_context
nodes.summary: Context for one failure mode's page, with its guards, causes, awaiting and planned packages linked.

nodes.name: saas_hits
nodes.summary: Returns guard terms found in raw page HTML after unescaping entities, normalising look-alike characters and removing allowed phrases.

nodes.name: internal_links
nodes.summary: Extracts the site-root paths a page links to or loads.

nodes.name: relative_links
nodes.summary: Extracts relative href/src values the link check cannot follow.

nodes.name: inline_scripts
nodes.summary: Extracts bodies of inline script tags for CSP hashing.

nodes.name: kinetic
nodes.summary: Context processor flagging KINETIC and BAUHAUS for the content pages, essays and home page.

nodes.name: csp_hash
nodes.summary: Computes the CSP sha256 source expression for an inline script body.

nodes.name: _rendered
nodes.summary: Renders every page in the page table through its view, collecting HTML and render failures.

nodes.name: _resolves
nodes.summary: Decides whether an internal link resolves to a page, a static file, a hosting file or a redirect.

nodes.name: _headers
nodes.summary: Builds the Cloudflare _headers file with a Content-Security-Policy hashing all inline scripts.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Writes the full static site to a marked folder, or returns problems (render failures, broken or relative links, online-service wording) and writes nothing.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Django BaseCommand exposing build_static --out and raising CommandError listing any problems.

nodes.name: essay_path
nodes.summary: Maps an essay URL name to its /essays/ path.

nodes.name: public_paths
nodes.summary: Lists the site path of every public page.

nodes.name: Page
nodes.summary: Frozen record for a public page: URL name, namespace, path, kind and source.

nodes.name: _home
nodes.summary: Home page context: lattice, table, headline evidence, learned change, sweep extremes, speed and the narrative limits linked to components and essays.

nodes.name: _components
nodes.summary: Components page context from the catalogue, extensions, vetting and premortem failure modes.

nodes.name: _graph
nodes.summary: Repository graph page context read from the static knowledge-graph.json and meta.json.

nodes.name: template_page
nodes.summary: Renders a template page with its render-time context builder, if any.

nodes.name: _diagrams
nodes.summary: Turns mermaid code fences into escaped figure blocks with captions, leaving other fences untouched.

nodes.name: markdown_html
nodes.summary: Renders Markdown as the site does: strips front matter, filters planned text, draws diagrams and rewrites .md links to site URLs.

nodes.name: render_markdown
nodes.summary: Renders a content/*.md file to HTML and extracts its first heading as the title.

nodes.name: markdown_page
nodes.summary: View rendering a Markdown content page into the markdown_page template.

nodes.name: placeholder_page
nodes.summary: View rendering a placeholder page with its title.

nodes.name: failure_mode_page
nodes.summary: View rendering one failure mode's page from the failure map.

nodes.name: view_for
nodes.summary: Returns a Django view closure dispatching a Page to the view for its kind.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Guide to the g6solver.com Django site, which is built to static files with no database, accounts, cookies or analytics: how to preview it, where pages, Markdown content, static assets and the Tailwind build live, how build_static exports the site with a hashed Content-Security-Policy, how to refresh the embedded repository graph, and which tests cover the site.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Private npm manifest for the site's CSS build, pinning tailwindcss 3.4.17 and defining css:build and css:watch scripts that compile src.css into ../static/css/main.css.

nodes.name: src.css
nodes.summary: Tailwind source stylesheet for the site: base layer, a large components layer (glass panels, gradient text, numbered items, architecture stack, price rows, minimal footer, header, mobile menu and nav buttons) and a utilities layer, compiled into static/css/main.css.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Tailwind's @tailwind directives and @layer base/components/utilities so custom classes are ordered and purged with the generated utilities.

nodes.name: tailwind.config.js
nodes.summary: Tailwind configuration that scans the site's templates and static scripts for class names and extends the theme with the g6 colour palette and Inter / Geist Mono font stacks.
nodes.languageNotes: CommonJS module.exports with a JSDoc @type annotation for editor type-checking of the Tailwind Config.

nodes.name: 404.html
nodes.summary: Not-found page extending base.html with an error message and a link back to the landing page; build_static writes it out as the static site's 404.html.

nodes.name: base.html
nodes.summary: Root Django layout for every site page: head metadata (description, Open Graph, Twitter, canonical URL from request.path, JSON-LD SoftwareSourceCode), favicons, fonts and stylesheets, optional kinetic and Bauhaus themes, the navbar, footer and gelly includes, and the site scripts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a {% comment %} block rather than {# #} for a multi-line note, since Django's single-brace-hash comment is single-line only and would render verbatim.

nodes.name: base_post.html
nodes.summary: Intermediate layout for essay pages that extends base.html and replaces the JSON-LD block with a schema.org BlogPosting built from each post's headline, date and description blocks.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Essays index page extending base.html that groups the research essays into themed clusters (such as The Intelligence Gap and The Cognition Argument) as linked cards using blog: URL names.

nodes.name: ai_cant_think.html
nodes.summary: Essay "AI Can Talk - But It Can't Think" arguing that a missing cognitive layer separates fluent LLM output from reasoning, and that G6 supplies that infrastructure.

nodes.name: ai_needs_middleware.html
nodes.summary: Essay "The Operating System Analogy: Why AI Needs Middleware" comparing raw LLMs to bare-metal hardware and arguing for shared cognitive middleware for reasoning, memory, checking and self-monitoring.

nodes.name: algorithms_missing_intelligence.html
nodes.summary: Essay "Algorithms Are the Missing Intelligence" arguing that systems should select, compose and synthesise explicit algorithms at runtime, using ML only for ambiguity.

nodes.name: alignment_is_engineering.html
nodes.summary: Essay "The Alignment Problem Is an Engineering Problem" framing alignment as systems engineering with explicit specs, formal methods, bounded operation and continuous monitoring.

nodes.name: antifragile_ai.html
nodes.summary: Essay "Antifragility in AI: Systems That Improve Under Stress" contrasting fragile, robust and antifragile AI systems and arguing for designs that learn from failure.

nodes.name: augmentation_not_replacement.html
nodes.summary: Essay "The Human-AI Team: Augmentation, Not Replacement" arguing that structured human-AI collaboration beats full automation for knowledge work and that interface design is the hard problem.

nodes.name: context_window_is_not_memory.html
nodes.summary: Essay "The Context Window Is Not Memory" arguing that long context is a buffer and that real memory needs structured stores, retrieval and consolidation.

nodes.name: democratising_agi.html
nodes.summary: Essay "Democratising AGI: Who Gets to Build Intelligence?" proposing user-built cognitive infrastructure on top of any model as an alternative to concentration in a few frontier labs.

nodes.name: economics_of_intelligence.html
nodes.summary: Essay "The Economics of Intelligence: Why AI Gets Cheaper When It Thinks" arguing that turning inference into reusable algorithms reverses per-token pricing and lock-in economics.

nodes.name: epistemology_of_ai.html
nodes.summary: Essay "What Epistemology Teaches Us About AI Knowledge" arguing that LLMs hold associations rather than justified beliefs and need explicit provenance, confidence and evidence infrastructure.

nodes.name: formal_verification_safety_net.html
nodes.summary: Essay "Formal Verification: The Safety Net AI Doesn't Use" arguing for applying SAT/SMT, model checking and theorem proving to the cognitive layer of high-stakes AI systems.

nodes.name: hallucination_is_design.html
nodes.summary: Essay "The Hallucination Problem Is a Design Problem" arguing that hallucination follows from optimising token probability over truth and that generation should be separated from checking.

nodes.name: learning_without_forgetting.html
nodes.summary: Essay "Learning Without Forgetting: The Continual Learning Problem" arguing that fine-tuning is destructive and that systems need architectures that learn additively.

nodes.name: map_is_not_territory.html
nodes.summary: Essay "The Map Is Not the Territory: Statistical Models vs. Understanding" on recognising when a model's learned map of language diverges from reality.

nodes.name: metacognition_missing_skill.html
nodes.summary: Essay "Metacognition: The Skill AI Doesn't Know It's Missing" arguing that AI lacks the ability to monitor, evaluate and regulate its own cognition and so cannot tell confident answers from confabulations.

nodes.name: move_fast_break_things.html
nodes.summary: Essay "Why 'Move Fast and Break Things' Doesn't Work for AI" arguing that speed and safety are compatible only when safety is architectural rather than procedural.

nodes.name: periodic_table_of_intelligence.html
nodes.summary: Essay "The Periodic Table of Intelligence", the longest in the batch, framing intelligence as a composition of discrete cognitive primitives with known properties and failure modes that can be catalogued and composed.

nodes.name: scaling_laws_ceiling.html
nodes.summary: Long-form essay 'Scaling Laws Have a Ceiling' arguing that neural scaling power laws carry diminishing returns, so further gains must come from architecture rather than scale; extends the blog post base template and fills its headline, date and description blocks.

nodes.name: self_improvement_safety.html
nodes.summary: Essay 'Self-Improvement Without Self-Destruction' arguing that safe self-modification belongs in an explicit, inspectable layer rather than in opaque model weights; a blog post built on the shared post base template.

nodes.name: two_types_of_thinking.html
nodes.summary: Essay 'The Two Types of Thinking and Why AI Only Has One' applying Kahneman's dual-process framework to argue current AI lacks slow deliberation and needs architectural change; a blog post on the shared post base template.

nodes.name: why_benchmarks_lie.html
nodes.summary: Essay 'Why Benchmarks Lie' arguing that AI benchmarks measure pattern recall rather than real-world capability (Goodhart's Law) and proposing process-oriented evaluation; a blog post on the shared post base template.

nodes.name: cta_button.html
nodes.summary: Reusable include for a gradient call-to-action link button parameterised by url, text and size; no current template includes it, so it appears to be a leftover from the earlier Tailwind site design.

nodes.name: feature_card.html
nodes.summary: Reusable include for a glass-style feature card taking icon_svg, title, description and color_class; no current template includes it, so it appears to be a leftover from the earlier Tailwind site design.

nodes.name: footer.html

layers.name: Core Foundation
layers.description: The shared base every G6 package builds on: the AIBlock component contract, reliability envelopes, ledgers, consent registry, sandbox confinement, failure-mode catalogues, provider allowance records, file-integrity manifests and envelope invariants.

layers.name: MCP Server and Entry Surfaces
layers.description: The surfaces agents and people call G6 through: the MCP server (registrations, consent, review loop, composition), the setup and doctor commands, runnable bundles with their own server, the using-g6 skill and the navigator that checks and runs plans against the registry.

layers.name: Review Harness and Workforce
layers.description: The patch-review and checking harness: harness and workforce runs that review a coding agent patch, the metaharness that measures and adapts harnesses, the coding-agent gate, reliability pipeline, operator loop, goal trees, self-maintenance planning and the learning, self-training and distillation that feed improvement back in.

layers.name: Evidence and Action Control
layers.description: Components that decide whether a claim or action may proceed: action gating and action logic, the safety engine, safety bounds over Markov agent models, epistemic integrity, evidence grading, grounding, guards and intent checks.

layers.name: Reasoning and Formal Methods
layers.description: Checkable reasoning engines and formal tools: Lean, Prolog and Datalog adapters, model checking, counterexample-guided synthesis, solvers, algebra, causal and graph reasoning, optimisation, complexity analysis, debate, provers, abstraction engineering and algorithm design.

layers.name: Cognitive Architectures and Agents
layers.description: Agent-facing cognition: cognitive architectures, the cognitive bridge from intent to method, agent components, embodied motion and sensor checks, memory, the local-first model router and the research programmes built on them.

layers.name: Knowledge and Context
layers.description: Knowledge and context sources G6 reasons over: the knowledge family, source connectors, context components, the Context Engine that serves the g6_knowledge MCP tools, and the shared-file workspace family.

layers.name: Domain Extension Families
layers.description: Applied extension families for specific kinds of work: media, machine-learning and code components, duty-of-care jobs with their instrument data and certificates, deployment plans, professional-standards domains and integrations with outside systems.

layers.name: Validation Studies and Guides
layers.description: Evaluation studies under validation/ (a benchmark of real coding issues, patch review, metaharness, grounding and action-gating runs with their fixtures), runnable demos and cognitive-bridge examples, and the top-level README and agent guide.

layers.name: Django Site
layers.description: The project Django site: manage.py, g6site settings and URLs, the pages app, Django templates, site content and catalogue data, and the Tailwind stylesheet build.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README: G6 is an open-source library of checkable AI components for reasoning, evidence, checks and action control, in early alpha. Its first use is patch review: before a coding agent says a Python change is done, it calls g6_review_patch, and G6 runs the requirement tests inside an operating-system boundary and reports what it reproduced. The README also introduces the three result labels (verified, qualified-draft, blocked-escalated) and the rule that G6 never upgrades a label it did not earn; every later step of the tour comes back to that rule.

tour.title: The MCP Server Front Door
tour.description: The MCP server is the main way agents reach G6. src/g6/mcp/__init__.py builds the g6-mcp stdio server and registers its tools: discovery, invoke and compose, patch review, missions, consent, Context Engine and workflow records, with every reply wrapped in the shared envelope. review_reply.py shows a practical concern: the full patch review reply is saved to the state folder and a compact form is returned so it fits a client's tool-result limits. AGENT_GUIDE.md and the using-g6 skill are the instructions an agent reads to use these tools in the intended order.
tour.languageLesson: FastMCP servers register Python functions as tools with decorators; the function's signature and docstring become the tool schema the client sees, and stdio transport means the client launches the server as a child process and talks over stdin/stdout.

tour.title: Package Root, CLI and Setup
tour.description: The same capabilities are reachable from Python and the command line. src/g6/__init__.py declares the version and the public g6.invoke door, and src/g6/cli/__init__.py defines the g6 command's subcommands (setup, components, describe, invoke, doctor and more). g6 setup asks once per computer whether code may run without an operating-system boundary and registers the MCP server from Step 2, while g6 doctor is a read-only check of the installation, including whether an isolation backend is present.

tour.title: The AIBlock Component Contract
tour.description: Every surface from Steps 2-3 ends up calling components, and every G6 component is or wraps an AIBlock. ai_block.py defines the infer/verify/contract hooks and >> chaining, where a PipelineBlock folds per-stage evidence and keeps the weakest completion state. Each block edge returns the railway-style Result from result.py, and the @block_contract and maturity decorators attach a declared purpose, inputs, failure modes and maturity level to each component class; these are among the most imported files in the project.
tour.languageLesson: Class decorators in Python run at import time and can attach metadata to the class object itself, so a registry can later read a component's contract without instantiating it. A railway-oriented Result type (ok/fail with map and flat_map) makes failure an ordinary return value instead of an exception.

tour.title: Labels, Envelopes and the Door
tour.description: This step is the code behind the README's label rule. g6.core (the most depended-on module in the graph) defines the canonical labels, reliability_envelope.py carries state, warning cards and evidence across every surface and applies a down-only promotion law, and door.py is the rule each door applies to a component's own claim. A `verified` label stands only when G6's own re-checker reproduces the check; otherwise the result is held at qualified-draft, and a mismatch blocks.
tour.languageLesson: A module-level __getattr__ (PEP 562) lets a package resolve names lazily on first access, so importing g6.core stays side-effect-free and cheap while still exposing AIBlock, Result and friends as attributes.

tour.title: File Integrity: The Re-check Path
tour.description: The README notes that the one path that can currently return the verified label is the file-integrity check called from Python with the caller's own pin. integrity/__init__.py builds SHA-256 manifests and compares a tree against one, and tree.py is G6's own re-checker: it re-hashes the files, compares them with the manifest and the pin, and plants two perturbation controls the check must catch. It is a compact worked example of the door rule from Step 5.

tour.title: Registry, Composition and Plans
tour.description: With the block contract in place, registry.py discovers components lazily from the installed package and entry points, tracks name collisions and invokes a block's infer op within a parameter budget. compose.py wires registered blocks into a ComposedBlock, checking required inputs, wiring and evidence kinds, and mcp/composition.py exposes that as a data-only MCP tool. The navigator package checks and runs multi-step plans against the same registry and contracts.

tour.title: Durable State, Ledgers and Stop
tour.description: G6 keeps its records in one place and in a form that can be re-checked later. storage.py defines the single state root ($G6_HOME, default ~/.g6) and the path-containment checks that refuse traversal, symlink, junction and network paths. ledger.py is an append-only, hash-chained JSON ledger that recomputes every hash and refuses forks from concurrent writers, and stop.py is the process-wide stop switch that the door, the safety engine and harness runs consult before starting new work.
tour.languageLesson: In a hash-chained log each entry stores the hash of the previous entry, so editing or removing any past entry changes every later hash; re-verifying means recomputing the chain from the start and comparing it with an expected head.

tour.title: The Operating-System Boundary
tour.description: Patch review runs code an agent wrote, so it needs isolation. confine.py plans a per-run Windows AppContainer or Linux bubblewrap sandbox with explicit read-only and read-write grants and explains refusals with the owner's fix. outside.py declares programs and local services the person installs themselves and reaches them only over loopback, and repo_tests.py reads the caller's git repository with hardened read-only calls and runs its pytest tests confined, at the patch and at the base revision, returning stable G6_E_* refusals.
tour.languageLesson: Python's ctypes module calls native OS APIs (here the Windows AppContainer functions) directly from Python, without a compiled extension; the cost is that struct layouts and error codes must be declared by hand.

tour.title: Patch Review: The First Use
tour.description: patch_review.py is the reference application behind g6_review_patch and one of the files with the widest fan-out in the codebase. It runs the checks confined (Step 9) at the patch and base commits, detects test weakening (the safety engine package re-exports a static test-weakening check), enforces the person's confirmed expectations through confirmed_checks.py, and returns its result in the envelope from Step 5. The harness package entry defines Check and Standard and the intake, plan, execution, adjudication and memory spine, and behaviour_runner.py is the isolated runner that reads back exactly one bounded observation frame.

tour.title: Completion Loop and Coding Missions
tour.description: A single review becomes a loop when the agent fixes what G6 reproduces and asks again. completion_loop.py runs hidden probes and a critic's review-until-clean rounds against claimed-finished work until it holds or a stop rule fires, and mcp/review_loop.py exposes one step per MCP call. The workforce package frames a local coding mission under a frozen standard (scope, clarification, execution permission, repair ladder), and evidence/certificate.py is the single issuer that decides a mission's completion state from checks, negative controls and receipts on the exact artifact bytes.

tour.title: Model Calls and Cloud Consent
tour.description: Patch review makes no model call unless the caller turns one on, and llm.py is the single explicit seam for any model call, with local, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic and fake callers. Before user data reaches a cloud model, core/cloud_consent.py runs one admission check against a lock-serialised ledger of grants, revocations and disclosures, and consent_registry.py routes every model handed through the door through that guard. On the MCP side, mcp/consent.py and mcp/cloud_consent.py ask the person through the client's dialog, per source and provider, and withhold content that has no grant.

tour.title: Agents and Action Control
tour.description: G6 also runs agents and decides whether their proposed actions may proceed. run.py (the highest-scoring code entry point in the analysis) defines the AgentRuntime protocol and run_agent, which checks stop and limits before each event and turns every failure into a blocked-escalated outcome. gate.py's ToolGate decides run, dry_run or refused for every tool call, drawing on the action gate's decision_engine.py, which folds precondition, scope and safeguard checks into a GateDecision with reason codes. The epistemic-integrity adjudicator applies the same discipline to claims, grading declared evidence and capping confidence by grade.
tour.languageLesson: typing.Protocol defines structural interfaces: any adapter class with the right methods satisfies AgentRuntime without inheriting from it, which lets wrappers for different agent frameworks share one runner.

tour.title: Metaharness and Validation Studies
tour.description: The metaharness measures and adapts harnesses themselves, with the widest fan-out of any file in the graph. api.py is the adapt entry point (confirm, propose, diagnose, baseline, evaluate, decide, activate, roll back), returning expected failures in the envelope rather than raising them, and loop.py is a shadow self-improvement tick that names the costliest constraint and gates candidates in its own workspace. The V7 SWE-bench protocol under validation/ shows how such questions are posed as studies with stated arms and oracles, which ties back to the README's caution that application-level benefits have not been established.

tour.title: The Django Project Site
tour.description: The last stop is outside the library: web/ is the static Django site for the project. manage.py previews it with runserver or exports it with build_static, settings.py configures a site with no database, sessions or accounts, and views.py renders one view per page kind from templates and Markdown content. clients.py holds the per-client instructions for connecting agents to the g6-mcp server from Step 2, closing the loop between the documentation and the code.
tour.languageLesson: Django can serve a site with no database at all: dropping the auth, sessions and admin apps from INSTALLED_APPS and rendering templates from files lets the same project run as a local preview server or be exported to static HTML.
